articles.headline: Microsoft apologizes for global outage disrupting products for nearly 24 hours
articles.title: Microsoft says services fully restored after for day-long global outage
articles.summary: Technology giant Microsoft issued a profound apology for a massive technical failure affecting Microsoft 365 products globally across more than seventy countries. The disruption began on Thursday and lasted nearly 24 hours, impacting operations for businesses, government services, and hundreds of millions of users worldwide before services steadily recovered by Friday afternoon following a network capacity upgrade.
articles.description: Efforts to address the underlying problem with Outlook, Teams and Copilot are complete, the tech firm says.

articles.headline: Trump, Putin and Xi plan historic joint meeting in China next week
articles.title: Trump, Putin and Xi plan historic joint meeting in China next week, White House says
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian leader Vladimir Putin plan to hold a trilateral meeting next week during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, according to White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales. The leaders of the world's largest nuclear powers will discuss reducing nuclear weapons and the war in Iran, while bilateral talks are also scheduled between Trump and Xi.
articles.description: Trump will discuss the "reduction of nuclear weapons" during the unprecedented talks, a spokeswoman says.

articles.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin to hold first three-way summit in China
articles.title: Trump, Xi and Putin to hold first three-way summit in China
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian leader Vladimir Putin will hold a three-way meeting next week during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China, according to the White House. The unprecedented talks follow the expiration of the New Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty in February, though a senior US official stated no agreement is expected from the discussions.
articles.description: White House says Trump plans to discuss the Iran war and nuclear arms at a meeting on the sidelines of APEC next week.

articles.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin plan unprecedented joint meeting in China
articles.title: Trump, Xi and Putin plan unprecedented joint meeting on sidelines of APEC in China: officials
articles.summary: Leaders of the United States, China and Russia plan to meet on November 19, 2026, in Shenzhen during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. The White House confirmed the unprecedented trilateral gathering involving Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin. Analysts suggest the talks will be largely symbolic rather than yielding major breakthroughs. Discussions are expected to cover nuclear arsenals and the war with Iran.
articles.description: For the Kremlin, the planned trilateral meeting is a coveted chance to posture as a superpower on par with Washington and Beijing

articles.headline: Donald Trump to discuss nuclear arms cuts with Putin and Xi
articles.title: Donald Trump to raise nuclear-arms cuts with Putin, Xi on November 19, White House says
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump will raise nuclear arms reduction during a November 19 meeting in Shenzhen, China, with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping. White House spokesperson Olivia Wales announced the talks on November 13, 2026. Beijing has historically resisted bilateral nuclear discussions with Washington, and a senior administration official stated that no immediate formal agreement is anticipated from the gathering.
articles.description: Vladimir Putin, Xi Jinping and Donald Trump are expected to meet on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum in Shenzhen

articles.headline: U.S. flights grounded nationwide due to telecommunications outage
articles.title: U.S. flights resume after hours-long outage as FAA lifts nationwide ground stop
articles.summary: All departing flights across the United States were grounded on Friday, November 13, 2026, following a temporary telecommunications outage affecting air route traffic control centres. The Federal Aviation Administration ordered the rare national stop out of an abundance of caution, stranding tens of thousands of passengers and causing widespread travel disruption. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin confirmed there was no indication of a nefarious attack.
articles.description: Disruption not due to a cyberattack or a sweeping Microsoft outage, top officials said; the incident marked only the second time such an alert was given in U.S. airspace since the 9/11 attacks

articles.headline: FAA grounds all fights across the US over ‘telecommunication outage’
articles.title: FAA grounds all fights across the US over ‘telecommunication outage’
articles.description: The FAA has issued a ground stop for departing flights in the US after a communications failure disrupted air traffic.

articles.headline: US flights grounded nationwide following communication system failure
articles.title: US flights resume after FAA lifts hours-long nationwide ground stop
articles.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration grounded all flights across the United States after a communication issue impacted traffic control centres. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy confirmed technicians are investigating the disruption, which has caused approximately 7,000 cancellations or delays. This represents the first nationwide ground stop since January 2023, highlighting ongoing infrastructure challenges within the national aviation system.
articles.description: US officials say air control centres affected by 'communication issues', but no threat detected.

articles.headline: Global Microsoft outage disrupts email and cloud services worldwide
articles.title: Why is Microsoft's outage lasting so long and will emails be lost?
articles.summary: A widespread technical disruption affecting Microsoft 365 applications impacted hundreds of millions of users globally, causing connectivity failures for Outlook, Teams, and artificial intelligence tools. Technology companies, government agencies, and medical services experienced significant disruptions. Microsoft ruled out cyber-attacks, attributing the incident to elevated server loads, while experts warned of unprecedented business consequences.
articles.description: Microsoft says it is continuing to restore services including Outlook and Teams following a global outage.

articles.headline: Iran claims destruction of US military radar in Bahrain
articles.title: Iran says it struck U.S. military radar in Bahrain
articles.summary: The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps stated on November 13, 2026, that it destroyed an American early-warning radar installation in Bahrain. According to the Iranian military, the operation served as retaliation for a United States air strike targeting a telecommunications tower in Sirik. Meanwhile, U.S. President Donald Trump announced the halt of diplomatic talks with Tehran, reinforcing the naval blockade.
articles.description: The IRGC says the strait is closed, while the U.S. Navy claims that it has opened a southern route for commercial vessels to exit and enter the critical waterway, while maintaining its “ironclad blockade” of Iranian ports

articles.headline: Iran threatens unlimited response over Strait of Hormuz after US attack

articles.headline: Microsoft struggles to restore global services following major server outage
articles.title: Microsoft hit by global outages: What happened and why?
articles.summary: Technology giant Microsoft reported limited success in restoring widely used workplace applications more than twelve hours after a global technical failure disrupted Outlook and Teams across seventy-four countries. The corporation stated that servers experienced unexpected unavailability and elevated loads, prompting international government disruptions. Officials confirmed no evidence of malicious cyber activity behind the ongoing server failures.
articles.description: Outlook, Teams and Copilot remain disrupted in 74 countries as Microsoft reports ‘marginal success’ in fixing outage.

articles.headline: Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang resigns following reports of extramarital affairs
articles.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns amid spy scandal
articles.summary: Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang stepped down as president, chief executive, and board member on Thursday, November 12, 2026, after acknowledging extramarital relationships, including one with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset. Chief financial officer Colette Kress assumed the role of interim chief executive while the board considers permanent candidates. The departure has introduced uncertainty for the four trillion dollar artificial intelligence chipmaker amid falling share prices and ongoing national security investigations.
articles.description: Chief financial officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while keeping her finance role, and the board will consider internal and external candidates for a permanent replacement

articles.title: Watch: How Microsoft services went down around the world

articles.headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang quits following controversies over relationships
articles.title: Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang summoned to testify before Congress about affair with alleged Chinese spy
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence chipmaker Nvidia Corporation has lost billions in market value after chief executive Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday. His departure followed public revelations concerning extramarital relationships, including one with an executive and another alleged to involve a foreign intelligence asset. US lawmakers demanded answers regarding national security, while Colette Kress stepped in as interim chief executive officer.
articles.description: Huang abruptly quit on Thursday as head of one of the world's most valuable companies after revelations of alleged extramarital affairs.

articles.headline: Iran reports targeting American radar facility in Bahrain
articles.title: Iran says it targeted US radar site in Bahrain
articles.summary: Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps announced that it targeted a United States early-warning radar in Bahrain following an air attack on a telecommunications tower in southern Iran. State-aligned agencies reported the strike as a warning against aerial provocations in the Strait of Hormuz. The incident marks the first claimed attack on U.S. assets in a Gulf state since early September.
articles.description: IRGC says it hit radar in retaliation for an 'enemy' air attack on a telecom tower in Iran's Hormozgan province.

articles.headline: Finnish military detects strike on Russian warship
articles.title: Finland detects strike on Russian warship as Zelenskyy meets US envoys
articles.summary: Forces in Finland monitored a rare strike involving a Russian navy vessel within the Gulf of Finland area, though officials confirmed the Nordic country faced no immediate military threat. The development occurred alongside shuttle diplomacy efforts by United States envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, who met with leaders in Moscow and Ireland following trilateral negotiations in the United Arab Emirates.
articles.description: Reports of attack in Baltic came before US envoys met with Russian and Ukrainian presidents.

articles.headline: US envoys arrive in Moscow to discuss Ukraine war with Putin
articles.title: US envoys meet Zelensky in Dublin after talks with Putin in Moscow
articles.summary: American negotiators Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Wednesday to discuss European security and the ongoing conflict in Ukraine. The visit followed two days of talks in Abu Dhabi and preceded a planned trip to Dublin to brief Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky. Meanwhile, Ukrainian forces reported renewed connectivity issues with SpaceX service Starshield.
articles.description: US envoy Steve Witkoff says President Putin has agreed to European negotiators joining the next round of Ukraine talks.

articles.headline: Assam accident autopsy scheduled as chief minister visits victims
articles.title: Assam accident: Autopsy of 26 bodies on November 14; CM to visit injured, meet families of deceased
articles.summary: Authorities in Assam announced that autopsies for twenty-six individuals killed in a vehicle collision on November 13, 2026, will occur on November 14 at Swahid Kushal Konwar Civil Hospital in Golaghat. Minister Ranoj Pegu stated that seven critically injured patients remain in the intensive care unit at Jorhat Medical College Hospital. Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma plans to visit affected families in Golaghat district.
articles.description: Twenty-six people died in a head-on collision between the two vehicles at Rangajan on National Highway 715 near Kaziranga National Park on November 13

articles.headline: FAA air traffic control technology upgrade causes nationwide ground stop
articles.title: Trump administration blames ‘overloaded’ systems for ground stop after FAA lets flights resume
articles.summary: United States air traffic control systems experienced communications and radar gaps on November 13, 2026, due to new equipment overloading older infrastructure. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy confirmed the five-hour nationwide ground stop affected thousands of flights and over one million travelers before operations resumed on Friday night.
articles.description: Thousands of flights and potentially over a million travellers were affected from coast to coast

articles.headline: Yemeni city faces severe health crisis amid Houthi blockade
articles.title: Siege fuels disease fears in Yemen’s Taiz
articles.summary: The ongoing Houthi blockade in Taiz, Yemen, has triggered acute shortages of food, safe water, and medical supplies, severely restricting civilian access to hospitals. According to the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs, thousands of residents suffer from acute watery diarrhoea and suspected cholera as waste accumulates and sanitation trucks are blocked from reaching local landfills.
articles.description: Health officials warn that falling numbers of recorded infections may conceal a worsening disease crisis in Taiz.

articles.headline: Centre sanctions new infrastructure along China border in Arunachal Pradesh
articles.title: Why has Centre sanctioned fresh infrastructure along the China border in Arunachal Pradesh? | Explained
articles.summary: The Indo-Tibetan Border Police has sanctioned new infrastructure construction in Arunachal Pradesh amid ongoing face-offs with the Chinese Army along the Line of Actual Control since late July. This follows the February approval by the Cabinet Committee on Security for the third phase of the Indo-China Border Roads project to build twenty-six roads.
articles.description: The tension in Arunachal Pradesh has persisted even though India and China held three high-level border talks since July 2026

articles.headline: FAA ground stop disrupts NBA, NHL and college football weekend travel
articles.title: US lifts ground stop, but passengers face second day of flight disruption
articles.summary: More than 1.5 million air passengers and multiple sports teams faced travel chaos after the United States Federal Aviation Administration halted departing flights nationwide for over four hours due to a telecommunications outage. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy stated it will take time to restore capacity following the incident, which caused thousands of delays and cancellations before the ground stop was lifted at 8:15pm Eastern time on Friday.
articles.description: More than 1.5 million passengers face travel disruption as domestic and international airlines warn of knock-on delays.

articles.headline: Six people killed in Israeli airstrike on Nasser Hospital in Gaza
articles.title: Israeli strike on Gaza hospital kills six Palestinians, health ministry says
articles.summary: An official from the Hamas-run civil defence agency reported that an Israeli airstrike hit the surgery department of Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis, southern Gaza, killing at least six people and wounding twenty others. The strike occurred early on Thursday and caused extensive damage to the facility, while the Israeli military provided no immediate response.
articles.description: Witnesses say a missile hit a building containing the surgical wards and intensive care units at Nasser hospital, the largest in southern Gaza.

articles.headline: Germany parliament approves expanded operational powers for intelligence agencies
articles.title: German spies granted sweeping new powers
articles.summary: The German Bundestag passed legislation on November 13, 2026, granting the foreign intelligence agency BND and domestic service BfV powers to actively disrupt cyberattacks and hack adversaries. Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt supported the reform to counter foreign espionage, while opposition party Die Linke criticized potential privacy violations and historical parallels to East Germany's Stasi.
articles.description: Parliament passes legislation months after a thwarted attack at Leipzig-Halle airport, which Berlin linked to Russia.

articles.headline: Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles reports Q2 net loss of Rs 5,531 crore
articles.title: Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles reports Q2 net loss of ₹5,531 crore
articles.summary: Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles reported a consolidated net loss of Rs 5,531 crore for the second quarter ended September 30, 2026, driven by a one-time exceptional charge of Rs 6,738 crore and Jaguar Land Rover restructuring. Despite the loss, overall revenue rose thirty-five percent year-over-year to Rs 96,340 crore, supported by record domestic sales exceeding 200,000 units.
articles.description: The figures are not comparable because last year the company had exceptional gains due to the demerger of the company. During the period, the company’s revenue increased to ₹96,340 crore from ₹71,414 crore in the year ago period, up 35% YoY

Board chair Harvey Jones announced that chief financial officer Colette Kress will serve as interim chief executive officer during the search for a permanent successor. Kress addressed employees, acknowledging a difficult period and announcing a company meeting for November 18.
articles.description: Jensen Huang resigned as CEO of Nvidia this morning, a company he co-founded in 1993. articles.headline: US air traffic control system outage causes longest ground stop since 9/11
articles.title: What we know about the longest ground stop since 9/11
articles.summary: The United States Federal Aviation Administration lifted a nationwide ground stop that lasted more than four hours on Friday due to a communication issue affecting air traffic control centres. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy explained that analogue telecom switches and routers became overloaded with data, causing thousands of flight delays and cancellations in the longest nationwide stoppage since September 11, 2001.
articles.description: US officials say the disruption was caused by old equipment overloading and not a cyber-attack or a Microsoft outage.

articles.headline: PAHO revokes U.S. measles-free status after continuous transmission
articles.title: U.S. loses measles-free status after continued spread of the disease: report
articles.summary: The Pan American Health Organization stripped the United States of its measles-elimination status after 26 years due to uninterrupted virus transmission for over a year, according to a Wall Street Journal report on November 13, 2026. The nation faced roughly 7,500 infections and 13 deaths since 2025 amid declining immunizations, prompting the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention to record 5,182 confirmed cases across 45 states in 2026.
articles.description: The reported decision by the Americas branch of the ‌World Health Organization comes as the U.S. battles ‌the ⁠highest number of measles cases it has seen ⁠in more than three decades

articles.title: All passengers, crew on New Orleans cruise ship survive crash with tanker on Mississippi River
articles.summary: A tanker vessel collided with the river cruise boat American Heritage while it was docked near the port of New Orleans on Friday. The collision involved approximately 130 passengers on board and left the pleasure vessel partially submerged and listing. Local emergency services responded with rescue operations, though the precise cause of the collision and the extent of any injuries remained unclear immediately.
articles.description: Tanker owned by subsidiary of Chinese shipbuilder; too early to tell what might have caused the crash, but videos indicate some kind of catastrophic system failure on the vessel, a maritime law expert said

articles.headline: Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang steps down amid espionage allegations
articles.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns amid spy scandal and market loss
articles.summary: Colette Kress, chief financial officer and executive vice president, assumed the role of interim chief executive at Nvidia on Thursday after Jensen Huang resigned following scandals involving a suspected Chinese spy and a company executive. The tech giant appointed Harvey C. Jones as its first board chair as shares slid by approximately 10 percent on United States markets. The board convened following investigations by federal authorities and congressional panels into the security implications for advanced semiconductor exports.
articles.description: Tech giant's market value drops below $4 trillion after Huang steps down following espionage and affair allegations.

articles.headline: Nvidia leader Jensen Huang resigns after disclosures regarding extramarital affairs
articles.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns amid spy, affair scandals
articles.summary: Nvidia board members accepted the resignation of longtime president and chief executive Jensen Huang on Wednesday night following revelations of affairs with a suspected Chinese intelligence operative and an internal executive. Chief financial officer Colette Kress was appointed interim chief executive, while former Synopsys chief executive Harvey C. Jones became the company's first board chair. The departure places uncertainty on the microchip manufacturer's market dominance and political relationships following significant scrutiny.

articles.headline: Global Microsoft outage disrupts businesses and services worldwide
articles.title: Microsoft outage hits businesses worldwide; India feels impact
articles.summary: A global Microsoft disruption affecting Exchange Online and related services impacted businesses and public services worldwide on November 12 and 13, 2026. Indian enterprises, airlines, and international agencies experienced email and customer support delays. Microsoft reported recovery progress across affected infrastructure and stated it is investigating the root cause while addressing extensive message backlogs.

articles.headline: SpaceX to attempt double recovery of Starship rocket components
articles.title: Setback for SpaceX Starship rocket's double-catch test
articles.summary: SpaceX will attempt to catch both the Super Heavy booster and the Ship upper stage of its Starship rocket using mechanical arms during a test flight on Friday. The mission aims to demonstrate full reusability, which is critical for future Nasa lunar landings. The 124-metre rocket is scheduled to launch from Starbase in Texas.
articles.description: Elon Musk’s company aborted an attempted catch of the rocket’s booster - instead it came down in the ocean.

articles.headline: Xi Jinping declares Taiwan reunification inevitable during speech in Beijing
articles.title: Xi Jinping says Taiwan’s ‘complete reunification’ with China will happen
articles.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping stated on Thursday that Taiwan's reunification with China remains an unwavering historical mission that cannot be halted. Speaking at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing on the birthday of Sun Yat-sen, Xi reaffirmed adherence to peaceful reunification and the one country, two systems model. Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council promptly rejected the remarks, as the island's defense ministry reported detecting multiple Chinese military aircraft and warships conducting patrols nearby.
articles.description: Chinese president says the tide of history 'cannot be stopped' as Taiwan rejects 'one country, two systems'.

articles.headline: Amazon plans World Product Graph to index global online shopping data
articles.title: Amazon has a plan to index the world’s online shopping data
articles.summary: Amazon is reportedly planning to build the World Product Graph, a comprehensive data vault containing information on products sold anywhere across the internet. According to Reuters, the initiative aims to reduce user reliance on platforms like Reddit and Google while improving the accuracy of Amazon’s shopping assistant, Alexa for Shopping. Amazon stated that the internal document does not necessarily reflect current plans.
articles.description: Amazon has plans to build a vault of data on every product sold anywhere on the internet, even products Amazon doesn't sell, and make the information available through its own site, according to Reuters. articles.headline: Cruise ship passengers rescued following collision in New Orleans
articles.title: 'Miracle on Mississippi' - All passengers rescued after New Orleans cruise ship collision
articles.summary: Approximately 130 people aboard the American Heritage cruise ship were rescued after a collision with the cargo vessel Atlantic Asphalt on the Mississippi River in New Orleans on Friday. Thirty-two individuals sustained non-critical injuries and were hospitalised, while no people remained unaccounted for. Officials including Mayor Helena Moreno hailed the successful rescue operation as a miracle on the Mississippi.
articles.description: The collision leaves 32 people in hospital with non-critical injuries, but no-one unaccounted for.

articles.headline: Indian student protesters face heavy restrictions following summer demonstrations
articles.title: After a summer win, India's Gen Z protesters face a winter of uncertainty
articles.summary: Youth-led demonstrations in India have encountered severe police crackdowns and legal challenges as authorities move to curb dissent. Following a successful summer campaign that forced a federal minister's resignation, student activists now struggle to assemble. The governing party defends the restrictions, citing public order and legal boundaries, while legal experts and organizers warn that prolonged proceedings aim to deter opposition.
articles.description: A new wave of youth dissent swept India this summer, fuelled by frustration and irreverent online satire.

articles.headline: COP31 talks face sluggish climate finance responses amid Western security pressures
articles.title: Urgent climate finance pleas at COP31 face a non-urgent response
articles.summary: Urgent demands for climate finance from vulnerable developing nations met a slow response at the COP31 summit in Antalya as Western governments prioritized national security and domestic living costs. Host country Turkiye and Australia focused on implementing existing pledges rather than setting new targets. While multilateral development banks reported record lending in 2025, analysts noted significant funding gaps driven by geopolitical tensions, constrained fiscal spaces, and high capital costs.
articles.description: Climate action has slipped down the political agenda for Western governments as U.S. President Donald Trump has withdrawn international funding, while wars in Ukraine and West Asia have added to inflationary ‌pressures and the need to spend on security

articles.title: ChatGPT Wallet lets OpenAI’s Dots agents make purchases for you

articles.title: Microsoft says services still returning amid widespread outage

The server overload impacted global businesses, governments, and millions of subscribers using Microsoft 365 products. While the incident prompted widespread logistical challenges and forced some institutions to use alternative methods, the company stated the issue was not caused by cyberattacks.

articles.title: 'No light, no water, no heat': Ukrainians struggle with blackouts as Russia hits power grid
articles.summary: Millions of Ukrainians endure rolling blackouts lasting up to twenty hours daily following intensified Russian missile attacks on national energy infrastructure. DTEK chief executive Maxim Timchenko stated that the scale of destruction has left generating facilities severely degraded, while repair teams face persistent air raids that will delay full restoration until at least next summer.
articles.description: For parents in parts of Ukraine, trying to lead a normal family life with just a few hours of power each day is taking its toll.

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh secures ₹9.88 lakh crore in investments at Vizag summit

articles.headline: Bus and truck collision leaves 23 dead in Assam
articles.title: Students among 24 dead in bus-truck collision in Assam’s Kaziranga
articles.summary: At least twenty-three people were killed and twenty others injured following a head-on collision between a speeding minibus and a container truck on National Highway 715 near Kaziranga National Park in Assam. articles.description: Officials suspected that overspeeding by the minibus, travelling from Golaghat to central Assam’s Nagaon, caused the accident

articles.title: Ukraine fires nearly 1,200 drones at Russia as U.S.-led talks consider wider European security
articles.summary: Ukraine fired nearly 1,200 drones at Russian targets overnight in one of its largest aerial attacks, according to Russia’s Defence Ministry, resulting in seven deaths and seventeen injuries across three regions. Simultaneously, United States envoys held discussions in Abu Dhabi and Moscow regarding potential peace talks, agreeing to include wider post-Cold War European security arrangements. European Union leaders, including diplomatic chief Kaja Kallas, cautioned against Russian traps and insisted on prioritizing an immediate ceasefire.
articles.description: Kyiv's forces are using drones and ground robots to help defend against Russia's army along the about 1,200-km front line snaking down eastern and southeastern Ukraine

articles.headline: Armed men kill 37 civilians in western Niger ambush
articles.title: Armed men kill at least 37 civilians in western Niger, say local sources
articles.summary: Armed men killed at least 37 civilians in an ambush in western Niger on November 12, 2026, according to local sources. The attack targeted villagers travelling to a market in Tera within the Tillaberi region. The dead included members of a local self defence group and residents. Conflict monitors note the region is a jihadist violence epicentre.
articles.description: Ruled by a military junta since a 2023 coup, Niger is battling violence by jihadists linked to Al-Qaeda and the Islamic State group. Thousands have been killed in the violence over the last decade

articles.headline: Car bombings in Russia injure former Ukrainian adviser and kill military officer
articles.title: Car bombings in Russia kill military officer, injure ex-Ukraine PM adviser
articles.summary: A car bombing in Moscow critically injured Sergei Zavorotnyi, an adviser to former Ukrainian Prime Minister Mykola Azarov, after an explosive device detonated remotely under his vehicle on November 13, 2026. This followed a similar attack in St Petersburg that killed a Russian military serviceman. articles.headline: FBI states North Korean hackers stole four hundred million dollars via video calls
articles.title: North Korean hackers used fake video calls in $400m crypto hack, says FBI
articles.summary: State-sponsored hackers from North Korea stole more than four hundred million dollars in cryptocurrency from over 900 victims using fake video calls over an 18-month period, according to the Federal Bureau of Investigation. FBI cyber director Brett Leatherman stated that the scheme, dubbed FaceStealer, employs malware downloaded through imposter conferencing platforms to target cryptocurrency workers.
articles.description: More than 900 victims are thought to have fallen prey to the FaceStealer scheme in the last 18 months.

articles.headline: Trump considers military intervention against Cuba before leaving office in 2029
articles.title: Trump moots toppling Cuba authorities before leaving office
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump stated he would certainly consider using military force against Cuba during a phone interview with radio host Hugh Hewitt on Thursday. Trump expressed his desire to resolve the situation before his term ends in 2029, calling the island a failed nation. The announcement follows a de facto oil blockade and mounting sanctions imposed by Washington.
articles.description: Calling Cuba a failed nation, the US president hints at attack on the country before his term ends.

articles.headline: Donald Trump weighs potential military action against Iran following UN remarks
articles.title: Is Trump’s ‘no-war, no-peace’ plan on Iran sustainable?
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump considered potential military strategies regarding Iran, including a possible short and intense war targeting infrastructure after the November 3 midterm elections. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who lost his governing majority in October 27 elections, advocated for renewed air strikes alongside Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth and CENTCOM Commander Admiral Brad Cooper.
articles.description: Despite the U.S. President’s decision to hold off on further strikes, he remains neck-deep in the war he launched alongside Israel’s Netanyahu on February 28 this year

articles.headline: Yemen Houthis claim drone and missile strikes on Saudi infrastructure
articles.title: Yemen’s Houthis say they targeted Saudi East-West pipeline, port city of Yanbu
articles.summary: Yemen's Houthi movement stated on November 12, 2026, that its forces executed drone and ballistic missile attacks targeting the East-West pipeline, Yanbu port facilities, and Riyadh. The Saudi-led coalition reported intercepting multiple incoming drones and missiles across the kingdom during the same period, while civil defence officials noted debris falling near Mecca following the regional escalations.
articles.description: The East-West pipeline, which ends at Yanbu, has become increasingly important to Saudi Arabia, allowing it to get its oil to market after Iran blockaded the Strait of Hormuz on the other side of the Arabian Peninsula

articles.headline: Zelenskyy welcomes European Union inclusion in upcoming peace negotiations with Russia
articles.title: Zelensky welcomes US bringing Europe into Russia-Ukraine peace talks
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy praised a commitment from United States envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff to include European Union delegates in upcoming peace talks with Russia. Kushner and Witkoff met with Zelenskyy in Dublin on Thursday following discussions with Vladimir Putin in Moscow. Meanwhile, Zelenskyy reported that renewed restrictions on Starshield services are hindering military communications.
articles.description: The Ukrainian president says it makes sense for European leaders to be involved as Ukraine hopes to eventually join the EU.

articles.headline: Navi Mumbai named India's cleanest city in central government rankings
articles.title: Navi Mumbai recognised as India’s cleanest city in latest Swachh Survekshan
articles.summary: Navi Mumbai secured the top position as India's cleanest city during a central government awards ceremony, followed by Surat and Vijayawada. President Droupadi Murmu presented the accolades at the event. Ujjain led the three lakh to ten lakh population bracket, while Greater Visakhapatnam topped the ten lakh-plus category. Over 4,751 cities participated in the assessment conducted under the Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban initiative.
articles.description: Indore, ranked the cleanest city in the country for the past eight years, did not figure among the winners this year

articles.headline: India and Bangladesh postpone bilateral consular dialogue amid simmering tensions
articles.title: Amidst simmering tensions, India-Bangladesh consular dialogue postponed
articles.summary: The fifth India-Bangladesh consular dialogue, previously scheduled for November 17 and 18, has been postponed due to growing diplomatic tensions. The friction escalated after deposed Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina requested a new passport and national identity card through her legal representation in London. Acting Foreign Minister Humayun Kabir stated Dhaka would refuse the passport request and instead pursue her extradition, complicating bilateral relations and stalling normalization efforts.
articles.description: This would have been the fifth such consular dialogue and the first after the August 2024 uprising; postponement due to tensions over former PM Hasina’s plan to return to Bangladesh next month

articles.headline: Inaugurated church attacked in West Bengal village
articles.title: Bengal Church attacks: Choosing faith over fear
articles.summary: A newly inaugurated church in Narayantala village within the Basanti block of West Bengal was attacked by a group of people during its opening ceremony, injuring several attendees including a sixty-five-year-old woman. The incident occurred at the William Cary Memorial Church, prompting its immediate closure as authorities and local residents confront the aftermath of the violence that disrupted the community event.
articles.description: West Bengal has witnessed a sudden, rapid spike in attacks on Christian home fellowships and churches since the summer of 2026, when the BJP government came to power in the State. Senjuti Sengupta and Shiv Sahay Singh report on the fear of the community that is less than 1% of the population in West Bengal

articles.headline: Fighting continues in Ethiopia's Tigray region
articles.title: Neither war nor peace in Tigray - is Ethiopia's latest conflict really over?
articles.summary: Armed clashes and military operations persist across various areas of Ethiopia's northern Tigray region following a brief offensive by the national army and a strategic withdrawal by the Tigray People's Liberation Front. While federal supporters claim the conflict is effectively over, residents and security analysts report ongoing artillery fire and uncertainty as humanitarian concerns grow amid damaged infrastructure and widespread displacement.
articles.description: The army has taken control of most of Tigray's main towns - it is unclear if the TPLF is capable of fighting back.

articles.headline: Saudi-led coalition intercepts drones as UN extends sanctions
articles.title: Yemen’s Houthis renew strikes on Saudi Arabia as UNSC extends sanctions
articles.summary: Saudi-led coalition forces successfully intercepted suspected Houthi drones targeting the Riyadh region and Eastern Province, while the United Nations Security Council unanimously voted to extend sanctions on the group for another year. The military escalation involves cross-border attacks on oil infrastructure and military assets, prompting international calls for de-escalation as hundreds of thousands remain displaced across Yemen.
articles.description: Saudi-led coalition intercepts flurry of suspected Houthi drones targeting oil and military infrastructure.

articles.headline: Russian court sentences rights lawyer Maria Bontsler to prison for treason
articles.title: Russian court jails rights lawyer for 12 years on treason charge
articles.summary: A court in Kaliningrad sentenced sixty-six-year-old defence lawyer Maria Bontsler to twelve years in prison on Thursday. Prosecutors accused her of passing sensitive security information and details regarding criminal cases to Ukraine. The trial was held behind closed doors by the Federal Security Service, according to the rights advocacy group Slovo Zashchite, while her legal representatives maintained that the cited information was not secret.
articles.description: Prosecutors say the woman shared security details with Ukraine, while her lawyers argue the information was not secret.

articles.headline: Russia and Ukraine hold second day of U.S.-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi
articles.title: Russia, Ukraine hold second day of U.S.-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi
articles.summary: Delegations from Moscow and Kyiv held a second day of United States-brokered negotiations in Abu Dhabi on November 11, 2026, focusing on humanitarian issues and security guarantees. U.S. and Ukrainian officials reported constructive discussions, though no breakthrough occurred. Meanwhile, ongoing frontline fighting and overnight missile strikes caused civilian injuries and a fire at a Russian oil export port.
articles.description: ‘We are starting the second day of negotiations,’ Rustem Umerov, the head of Ukraine's Foreign Intelligence Service, who leads Kyiv's delegation in Abu Dhabi, says on social media

articles.headline: Pope Leo calls for Church to make ‘amends’ to sex abuse victims
articles.title: Pope Leo calls for Church to make ‘amends’ to sex abuse victims
articles.description: Pope Leo XIV says the Catholic Church must confront sexual abuse committed by clergy with truth and justice.

articles.headline: Karnataka government to seek Ninth Schedule inclusion for enhanced SC and ST reservations
articles.title: Karnataka to write to Prime Minister asking for inclusion of enhanced quota in Ninth Schedule
articles.summary: Following the Karnataka High Court quashing the 2022 reservation act, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar announced that the State government will write to Prime Minister Narendra Modi to include the enhanced quotas in the Ninth Schedule of the Constitution. Speaking on Thursday, Shivakumar added that a vision group and Cabinet sub-committee led by Deputy Chief Minister G. Parameshwara will review welfare programmes and manage pending central grants.
articles.description: After the High Court of Karnataka quashed the Karnataka Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Reservation of Seats in Educational Institutions and of Appointments or Posts in the Services under the State) Act, 2022, the State government will write to Prime Minister Narendra Modi to include the enhanced reservation for SCs and STs in the 9th Schedule of the Constitution

articles.headline: Russian warship reportedly struck by Ukrainian drone in Gulf of Finland
articles.title: Russian warship hit by Ukrainian drone in Gulf of Finland
articles.summary: Finnish and Estonian officials confirmed that a Russian warship was attacked in the Gulf of Finland on Wednesday during a broader Ukrainian drone operation targeting the Ust-Luga oil export depot. Ukraine's SBU security service stated the vessel was a Buyan-M type corvette, though Moscow has not detailed any damage or casualties. Estonian Defence Minister Martin Herem noted the ship emitted smoke before heading back towards St Petersburg.
articles.description: The attack is thought to be the first time Ukrainian drones have attacked a Russian ship in an open stretch of the Baltic Sea.

articles.headline: Palestinian infant dies from hypothermia in southern Gaza amid winter supply restrictions
articles.title: Palestinian baby dies from cold in Gaza amid Israeli restrictions on aid
articles.summary: A nine-month-old Palestinian baby named Kinan Ahmed Raqiq died from hypothermia in a Khan Younis tent after freezing temperatures hit the enclave overnight, according to his father and local medical personnel. The tragedy unfolded as Israel faces mounting international pressure from a coalition of more than fifty countries over severe restrictions on winter supplies, shelter, and fuel entering the war-torn territory.
articles.description: The baby's father said he died of hypothermia overnight in their family's tent in southern Gaza.

articles.headline: Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang resigns following revelations of extramarital affairs
articles.title: Why did Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resign, and who is Colette Kress?
articles.summary: Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang stepped down on Thursday following scrutiny over personal relationships, including an affair with a senior executive who reported directly to him. Chief financial officer Colette Kress has been appointed interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent replacement. The departure ends Huang's thirty-three-year tenure at the artificial intelligence chipmaking giant amid debates over US export restrictions to China.
articles.description: Huang has stepped down amid allegations of extramarital affairs and Chinese espionage.

articles.headline: Jensen Huang has resigned, what's next for Nvidia?
articles.title: Jensen Huang has resigned, what's next for Nvidia?
articles.description: The BBC's Samira Hussain reports from Wall Street on what the fall of the tech superstar means for the company and AI.

articles.headline: Student organisation condemns alleged sexual assault involving leader
articles.title: ABVP condemns sexual assault on Haldwani minor girl by its student leader and three others
articles.summary: The Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad condemned the alleged sexual assault of a sixteen-year-old girl in Haldwani, Uttarakhand, on November 13, 2026. Police arrested four suspects, including local student leader Dheeraj Bisht, who were reportedly members of the ITI Gang. State Secretary Yashwant Panwar stated that the RSS-affiliated organisation will assist the victim to ensure speedy justice.
articles.description: In a statement, the RSS-affiliated student organisation said it viewed the incident with "utmost seriousness" and would make every possible effort to ensure justice for the victim

articles.headline: Indian commerce minister begins two-day visit to boost ties in Egypt
articles.title: Piyush Goyal in Egypt: Both sides to discuss increasing cooperation in infra, manufacturing, logistics
articles.summary: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal arrives in Egypt on November 15, 2026, to co-chair the seventh session of the Joint Trade Committee alongside Minister Mohamed Farid Saleh. Accompanied by over 140 chief executive officers, Goyal will discuss bilateral trade, investment partnerships, and infrastructure cooperation. Bilateral merchandise trade between India and Egypt reached 5.04 billion dollars between April and September 2026.
articles.description: Egypt's strategic geographical location offers significant opportunities for Indian businesses to strengthen their presence in the country and access markets across Africa, the Middle East and Europe

articles.headline: Kurumba community in Kerala struggles to preserve unwritten language
articles.title: Kurumba: a language and community fighting for visibility
articles.summary: Classified as a Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, the Kurumbas reside in the hilly forest regions of Attappady within Palakkad district. Members primarily communicate using Kurumba, an oral language lacking a script. Because outsiders do not speak this language, community members must learn Malayalam and other regional languages for external communication.
articles.description: The Kurumbas of Keralam are an Adivasi community with a population of only 2,719 as of 2024, who speak Kurumba, an oral language without a script; with the Census classifying languages with fewer than 10,000 speakers as ‘others’, the future of the language appears bleak

articles.headline: Mohamed Salah becomes Egypt all-time leading scorer during Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers
articles.title: Salah breaks Egypt scoring record, Tunisia lose to Libya in AFCON qualifier
articles.summary: Mohamed Salah scored twice to become Egypt leading scorer with 70 goals as his national team defeated Malawi 5-0 on Friday in Cairo. In other matches, Morocco crushed Niger 5-1 in Casablanca, Nigeria beat Tanzania 3-1 in Uyo, Libya defeated Tunisia 2-0 at home, and South Africa drew 2-2 with Kenya. The tournament features cohosts Tanzania, Kenya and Uganda.
articles.description: Salah scored twice to take his international tally to 70 ​and surpass former captain Hossam Hassan’s record.

articles.headline: Indian envoy Vinay Mohan Kwatra hits back at USCIRF over Sharjeel Imam
articles.title: No locus standi: Indian envoy hits back at USCIRF for remarks on Sharjeel Imam
articles.summary: Indian Ambassador Vinay Mohan Kwatra criticized the United States Commission on International Religious Freedom on November 13, 2026, telling the bipartisan agency to introspect on its prejudices after it flagged the detention of Sharjeel Imam. Kwatra stated the commission has no locus standi to judge Indian citizens' rights, while Imam remains booked under the Unlawful Activities Prevention Act over allegations linked to the February 2020 Delhi riots.
articles.description: U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF) shared Sharjeel Imam’s profile on X, describing him as “a Muslim man detained in India for his religious freedom advocacy”

articles.headline: Kerala High Court rules police fully empowered to curb substance abuse in the city
articles.title: Police fully empowered to curb drugs and substance abuse in the city: Kerala High Court
articles.summary: The Kerala High Court stated that police possess full authority to enforce measures addressing drug and substance abuse across the state. A division bench comprising Justice Devan Ramachandran and Justice Basant Balaji considered a government appeal challenging a single-bench order regarding Kochi city police restrictions on hotel events. Legal representatives for Radisson Blu and the additional advocate general presented arguments during the proceedings.
articles.description: The court clarified that the directions issued by the Single Bench would not stand in the way of the police maintaining “requisite vigil and attention” to all activities about drug and substance abuse

articles.headline: Philippine court issues arrest warrant for jailed celebrity preacher Apollo Quiboloy
articles.title: Philippine court orders arrest of jailed, US-wanted celebrity preacher
articles.summary: A Philippine court issued an arrest warrant for detained celebrity preacher Apollo Quiboloy, who faces child sex trafficking charges in the United States. According to the Justice Department, the Makati Regional Trial Court acted following a formal extradition request made by Washington. Quiboloy denies all allegations against him, while currently remaining detained in Pasig without bail while on separate human trafficking trial proceedings.
articles.description: Palace denies timing of warrant is linked to Trump’s visit to Manila next week.

articles.headline: Central Bureau of Investigation conducts searches across six states in Mahadev betting app case
articles.title: Mahadev betting app case: CBI searches in 6 States lead to recovery of digital devices, key documents
articles.summary: The Central Bureau of Investigation executed searches at 33 locations across six states on November 14, 2026, recovering digital devices and documents related to the Mahadev online betting platform. Operations spanned Delhi, Mumbai, Nagpur, Amritsar, Bhopal, and Raipur based on disclosures from extradited promoter Sourabh Chandrakar. Officials stated that panel operators utilized mule bank accounts and hawala channels to transfer illegal profits abroad.
articles.description: The searches, carried out over the past few days, targeted premises in Delhi, Mumbai, Nagpur, Amritsar, Bhopal and Raipur, among others, linked to the betting platform's panel operators, they said.

articles.headline: Rubio criticizes international criminal court in speech
articles.title: Rubio assails international court in speech to conservative legal group
articles.summary: United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio criticized the International Criminal Court during an address to the Federalist Society in Washington on Friday, November 13, 2026. Rubio rejected international legal restraints on American actions, defended foreign policy decisions regarding Venezuela and Iran, and warned that Washington would respond forcefully if the Netherlands-based court pursued United States officials.
articles.description: The U.S., Mr. Rubio said, would not “submit to the sterile vision of radical judges or soulless global bureaucrats”

articles.headline: Kerala High Court directs Excise Commissioner to disclose underage alcohol consumption prevention steps
articles.title: Kerala HC directs Excise Commissioner to disclose steps taken to implement prohibitory measures to curb underage alcohol consumption
articles.summary: Justice A. Badharudeen directed the Kerala State Excise Commissioner to reveal actions taken for enforcing prohibitions against underage alcohol consumption. The petition filed by Vinod Vikraman Pillai of Kollam highlighted non-compliance with the Kerala Abkari Act regarding individuals under 23 years. The court noted recent fatal motor vehicle accidents involving minors and suggested the legislature consider lowering the juvenile age limit to 16 years.
articles.description: It was high time that the legislature considered appropriate amendments to the law to reduce the age of minority for juveniles and children in conflict with the law (CCL) to 16 years, the court opined

articles.headline: Oral GLP-1 medications offer new treatment options for diabetes and obesity
articles.title: Could one daily pill narrow the diabetes treatment gap in the Global South?
articles.summary: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist therapies are shifting from weekly injections to once-daily pills, potentially increasing global access to diabetes and obesity treatments. Oral options eliminate the need for cold-chain refrigeration, making distribution easier in emerging economies where high diabetes rates persist. Pakistan leads global prevalence at 31.4 percent, while medical experts highlight that these medications also improve cardiac, renal, and liver conditions.
articles.description: Globally, one in nine people lives with diabetes, as blockbuster injectable drugs begin making way for tablets instead.

articles.headline: Al Jazeera reports from Gaza hospital attacked by Israel
articles.title: Al Jazeera reports from Gaza hospital attacked by Israel
articles.description: Al Jazeera’s Tareq Abu Azzoum reports on the aftermath of an Israeli strike on Nasser Hospital

articles.headline: Jesus Owono suspended for 12 matches following Jesus de Miguel's death
articles.title: Goalkeeper Owono handed 12-match ban after De Miguel death
articles.summary: FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono received a 12-match suspension from the Spanish football federation on Friday after a collision during a second division match against Tenerife resulted in the death of forward Jesus de Miguel. De Miguel died in the hospital on November 3 at age 30. Spanish police have opened an investigation, and Owono withdrew from international duty with Equatorial Guinea.
articles.description: Owono and De Miguel ⁠collided during a Spanish second-tier match between FC Andorra and ​Tenerife on November 2.

articles.headline: UK government's Be Ready preparedness campaign sparks surge in emergency supplies
articles.title: Paranoid or practical? Britain’s ‘Be Ready’ citizen campaign
articles.summary: The British government's new Be Ready campaign has driven a sharp increase in sales of emergency supplies across England and Wales since its October 22 launch. Led by the Cabinet Office and backed by Defence Secretary Wes Streeting, the initiative urges households to prepare for a 72-hour outage by stocking essentials like bottled water and tinned foods, though critics warn many cannot afford the reserves.
articles.description: People in England and Wales are rushing to buy tinned goods and wind-up radios - but what's it all for?

articles.headline: India reports 38% decline in tuberculosis mortality since 2015
articles.title: India records 38% drop in TB mortality since 2015: WHO report
articles.summary: India achieved a 38% reduction in tuberculosis mortality since 2015, surpassing the global average of 35%, according to the World Health Organization’s 2026 report. The Union Health Ministry attributed this progress to the National TB Elimination Programme, which utilizes AI-enabled diagnostics and nutritional support. Globally, 1.13 million people died from the infectious disease in 2025.
articles.description: World Health Organization’s Global Tuberculosis Report 2026 showed a total of 1.13 million people died from tuberculosis last year

articles.headline: Katerina Siniakova secures record sixth year-end WTA No. 1 doubles ranking
articles.title: Katerina Siniakova clinches a record sixth year-end WTA No. 1 doubles finish
articles.summary: Katerina Siniakova secured her record sixth year-end finish as the top-ranked doubles player on the WTA Tour, holding the position for 209 weeks as of November 9, 2026. The Czech Republic native achieved a 54-8 match record this year, winning seven doubles titles, including the French and US Opens with partner Taylor Townsend, and received her trophy on Friday.

articles.headline: U.S. envoys meet Putin at Kremlin following Abu Dhabi talks
articles.title: No compromise with Ukraine, Putin indicates to U.S. envoys during talks
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump's envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived at the Kremlin on November 12, 2026, to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin after mediating peace talks between Russian and Ukrainian delegations in Abu Dhabi. The discussions wrapped up with a prisoner exchange agreement but no breakthrough on hostilities. Mr. Kushner announced he would fly to Dublin to meet Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy later that day.
articles.description: The Russian President proposes a short-term ceasefire in a key frontline city in Donetsk; he also rules out agreeing to foreign troops being stationed in Ukraine

articles.headline: Indian student wins medal of excellence at international vocational competition
articles.title: How a mason’s son from Erode won a Medal of Excellence at WorldSkills 2026
articles.summary: M Surenthiran, a twenty-two-year-old civil engineering student from Erode, secured a Medal of Excellence in the plastering and drywall systems category at the forty-eighth WorldSkills Competition held in Shanghai, China, in September. The event brings together skilled youth globally, with India finishing tenth overall. Surenthiran prepared through district and national events funded by Tamil Nadu Skills and IndiaSkills.
articles.description: M Surenthiran has won a Medal of Excellence in Plastering and Drywall Systems at the 48th WorldSkills Competition in China. His exposure to construction work through his father, a mason, laid the foundation for this achievement

articles.headline: Himachal Pradesh approves financial assistance scheme for eligible women
articles.title: Himachal’s ₹1,500 allowance scheme: Who benefits and what’s the political impact? | Explained
articles.summary: The Himachal Pradesh government approved the Mukhya Mantri Apna Parivar Sukhi Parivar Yojna scheme during a cabinet meeting in Shimla chaired by Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu. Under the initiative, 3.50 lakh eligible women aged 18 to 59 will receive 1,500 rupees per month alongside 300 units of free electricity for beneficiary families across the state.
articles.description: What does the new Mukhya Mantri Apna Parivar Sukhi Parivar Yojna offer? Amid mounting debt concerns and Opposition criticism, will the government be able to ensure its smooth implementation?

articles.headline: BJP dismisses Rahul Gandhi's phone tapping allegations as baseless and absurd
articles.title: Rahul Gandhi ‘habitual liar’: BJP on Congress leader’s phone tapping allegation
articles.summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party criticized Lok Sabha opposition leader Rahul Gandhi on Friday after he alleged that Prime Minister Narendra Modi is tapping his phone because it contains proof against him. BJP spokesperson Tuhin Sinha called Gandhi a habitual liar who engages in hit-and-run politics by making unsupported claims without providing evidence to authorities.
articles.description: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi alleged that he has proof of allegations against Narendra Modi on his phone, which is being “tapped by the Prime Minister”

articles.headline: Israeli caretaker defence minister asserts coalition does not need opposition approval for strikes
articles.title: No need for Opposition approval to launch strikes, says Israel’s Katz
articles.summary: Israeli caretaker Defence Minister Israel Katz stated on November 12, 2026, that the outgoing coalition does not require opposition permission to launch military operations. The remark followed warnings from opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot and parliamentary committee head Avigdor Liberman against unilateral military action. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Eisenkot subsequently agreed to meet at the Prime Minister's office to discuss national security.
articles.description: Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot urged caretaker PM Netanyahu to show restraint, warning that force without a “direct and immediate threat” could have “disastrous consequences for Israeli democracy and citizens’ trust”

articles.headline: Karnataka Chief Minister urges Centre for fair Bengaluru Metro cost sharing
articles.title: Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar places Karnataka’s demands on stage with Prime Minister
articles.summary: Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar requested Prime Minister Narendra Modi on November 13 to ensure a fairer financial partnership, expedite approvals for the Bengaluru Metro Pink and Red lines, and provide assistance for agricultural drought losses amounting to ₹62,482 crore. Speaking in Bengaluru, Shivakumar highlighted the state's economic contributions and sought central intervention regarding sugarcane pricing and Western Ghats environmental notifications.
articles.description: Demands included a fairer financial partnership over Bengaluru’s Namma Metro, clearance for Mekedatu project, scrapping Kasturirangan Report and immediate drought relief

articles.headline: Donald Trump directs JD Vance to focus on domestic anti-fraud efforts
articles.title: Trump says U.S. does not ‘need a deal with Iran’
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump announced on November 12, 2026, that Vice-President J.D. Vance must concentrate entirely on domestic anti-fraud initiatives rather than pursuing negotiations with Tehran. The directive followed reports that Mr. Vance considered face-to-face talks with an Iranian security official. The ongoing conflict, sparked by February joint strikes, has devastated energy transit through the Strait of Hormuz and contributed to recent Republican midterm election losses.
articles.description: His comments came shortly after the Wall Street Journal reported that Vice-President J.D. Vance was mulling face-to-face talks with a top Iranian security official

articles.headline: Kia and suppliers plan second manufacturing plant in Andhra Pradesh
articles.title: Kia, suppliers plan $2 billion investment in second plant in Andhra Pradesh, targets 2030 production kickoff
articles.summary: South Korean automaker Kia and its suppliers intend to invest approximately $2 billion to establish a second manufacturing facility in Andhra Pradesh, with production slated to commence in early 2030, according to a company announcement on November 12, 2026. The memorandum of understanding signed with the state government will generate about 12,000 direct and indirect jobs. The Anantapur plant will produce internal combustion and electric vehicles, expanding annual capacity by 200,000 units.
articles.description: The investment is expected to create about 12,000 direct and indirect jobs, the ‌company said, after signing a memorandum of understanding with the State government

articles.headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang steps down, more affair details revealed
articles.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang steps down, more affair details revealed
articles.description: Now that Huang has stepped down, Al Jazeera’s Kristen Saloomey looks at the questions ahead for the company.

articles.headline: Gaza families struggle with severe winter cold and shelter damage
articles.title: ‘Her hands are as cold as ice’: Gaza families struggle to keep warm
articles.summary: Displaced families in Gaza City face severe challenges protecting children from winter temperatures amid damaged makeshift shelters and flooding, according to reports from November 2026. The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs stated that 94 percent of the population needs shelter assistance, while aid agencies face severe funding shortages. Recent storms have worsened conditions, exacerbating hypothermia risks and leaving basic winter clothing unaffordable for residents.
articles.description: Flooded tents and high prices leave Gaza families struggling to keep children warm as winter approaches.

articles.headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns following revelations of two affairs
articles.title: The rise and fall of Jensen Huang - how the tech superstar became mired in scandal
articles.summary: Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday following reports of two affairs, including a relationship with a businesswoman alleged to be a Chinese intelligence asset and another with an Nvidia colleague. The departure creates uncertainty for the chipmaker, which is central to the artificial intelligence sector and valued at nearly $4 trillion. Despite previous backing from United States President Donald Trump, the board accepted his resignation following the disclosures.
articles.description: Within days, Huang's status as a seemingly untouchable figure leading the global tech race has crumbled.

articles.headline: NIA probes Pakistani gangster over online radicalisation of Indian youths
articles.title: NIA to probe two terror cases in Punjab, U.P.
articles.summary: The National Investigation Agency registered a case on November 12, 2026, targeting Pakistan-based gangster Shahzad Bhatti and Inter-Services Intelligence agents for allegedly radicalising Indian youths through social media. Officials stated the suspects lured individuals with financial incentives to conduct disruptive acts, building upon an initial investigation launched by the Uttar Pradesh Anti-Terrorist Squad earlier in April.
articles.description: During the investigation, it emerged that Pakistani gangster Bhatti, Jatt and radical Pakistani YouTubers, allegedly acting on instructions from the ISI, were attempting to radicalise Indian youths and entice them with financial incentives

articles.headline: Jerusalem Daily: Gaza’s Nasser Hospital hit by Israeli air strike
articles.title: Jerusalem Daily: Gaza’s Nasser Hospital hit by Israeli air strike
articles.description: For the seventh time, Israel has targeted Gaza’s Nasser Hospital in an air strike.

articles.headline: Indian envoy slams US panel over remarks on Sharjeel Imam
articles.title: Indian envoy slams USCIRF over Sharjeel Imam remarks, says panel has 'no locus standi'
articles.summary: India's Ambassador to the United States Vinay Mohan Kwatra criticized the United States Commission on International Religious Freedom on November 14, 2026, stating the panel lacked standing to judge Indian citizens' rights after it described jailed activist Sharjeel Imam as a religious freedom advocate. Imam was arrested in January 2020 over Citizenship Amendment Act protests and later charged under anti-terror laws by Delhi Police.
articles.description: In a strongly worded post on X, Vinay Kwatra rejected the commission’s assessment, accusing it of making partisan and ill-informed observations about India’s commitment to religious freedom and equal rights

articles.headline: Former council chief urges Ladakh voters to choose development
articles.title: Should Ladakh be hub of agitation or development?: LAHDC-K’s former Chief Executive Councillor
articles.summary: Mohammad Jaffer Akhoon, former Chief Executive Councillor of the Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Council-Kargil, urged citizens on November 13, 2026, to prioritize regional development over protests as the Leh Apex Body continued an indefinite sit-in. Akhoon defended upcoming local elections and noted previous talks with the Ministry of Home Affairs on special status had made significant headway before protests intensified in Leh.
articles.description: As the sit-in protest in Leh continues, LAB co-chairman said the dharna will “intensify from November 14”

articles.headline: Former Nvidia CEO misled top lawyers about affair with Alice Huang
articles.title: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang misled top lawyer on affair with Alice Huang: report
articles.summary: Former Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang misled company executives, including general counsel Tim Teter and marketing chief Alison Wagonfeld, regarding his affair with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, according to sources and internal messages reviewed by Reuters. Huang resigned on November 12, 2026, following the revelation of his relationships and subsequent board investigations into Alice Huang over potential spying suspicions.
articles.description: During the autumn of 2025 and in October 2026, in ‌response to press queries that drew some Nvidia leaders’ attention to his relationship with Megaspeed and Alice ​Huang, Jensen Huang at both times described their interactions as appropriate

articles.headline: SpaceX launches 15th Starship flight aiming for first round trip
articles.title: SpaceX launches 15th Starship flight with hopes of achieving first round trip
articles.summary: SpaceX launched its 15th uncrewed Starship spacecraft from South Texas on November 13, 2026, aiming to achieve the first successful orbital round trip and tower catch. While the upper stage reached orbit to deploy Starlink satellites, the Super Heavy booster deviated from its flight path and exploded over the Gulf of Mexico, marking a setback for Elon Musk's reusable rocket development program funded partly by NASA.
articles.description: Starship expected to descend from space after completing 14 orbits around Earth, setting up its debut catch landing for ​Saturday afternoon; the Super Heavy booster was diverted from its return flight path to a fixed point over the Gulf of Mexico before exploding a short distance ‌over the sea surface

articles.headline: International Criminal Court halts US troops probe in Afghanistan
articles.title: ICC stops probe into alleged crimes by US troops in Afghanistan
articles.summary: Judges at the International Criminal Court halted investigations into alleged crimes by American troops and ISIL in Afghanistan, citing evidence collection limitations. The ruling follows disputes with Washington over sanctions. The prosecutor appealed the decision while United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio previously vowed to dismantle the court, though the United States does not recognise its jurisdiction.
articles.description: The decision follows feuds between the United States and the Hague-based International Criminal Court.

articles.headline: International carriers object to Mumbai airport relocation proposal
articles.title: Why are international airlines being asked to shift to Navi Mumbai? | Explained
articles.summary: The International Air Transport Association wrote to the Ministry of Civil Aviation on September 9 objecting to Adani's Mumbai International Airport proposal. The plan requires shifting one-third of passenger and cargo movements to Navi Mumbai International Airport from October 1, 2026. The association opposed the forced relocation, which would cut 265 weekly international departures and affect 46 carriers.
articles.description: What has triggered the dispute between airport operator Adani Group and foreign carriers? How has Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis stepped in to challenge the proposed shift?

articles.headline: Fear of diagnosis keeping people away from diabetes screening, finds IDF survey
articles.title: Fear of diagnosis keeping people away from diabetes screening, finds IDF survey
articles.description: While 84% of the 502 adults surveyed in India felt a diabetes risk check was worthwhile even if they were healthy, only 14% believed they were likely to develop Type 2 Diabetes

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh launches Amaravati Quantum Valley innovation blueprint
articles.title: From policy to talent: Amaravati Quantum Valley’s innovation blueprint
articles.summary: Andhra Pradesh introduced a dedicated Quantum Policy to make Amaravati a top global quantum hub by 2030, combining research, commercial applications, and workforce training. Backed by Chief Minister Nara Chandrababu Naidu and Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the region attracted national agencies, global corporations, and startups while skilling over one hundred four thousand professionals to build a self-sustaining ecosystem.
articles.description: To put Amaravati among the top five global quantum hubs by 2030, competing alongside established centres in Chicago, Munich, Singapore, and Australia, Andhra Pradesh started with regulation

articles.headline: Justice Karnan’s incident brought judicial misconduct to the forefront
articles.title: Justice Karnan’s incident brought judicial misconduct to the forefront
articles.description: Two problems were raised in the aftermath — The need to revisit the process of selection/appointment of judges to constitutional courts, the need for an alternative to removal process to tackle judicial misconduct.

articles.headline: Amaravati Quantum Valley aims to build South Asia deep tech hub
articles.title: Inside Amaravati’s pioneering leap to quantum frontier
articles.summary: Engineers and policymakers in Amaravati are developing the Amaravati Quantum Valley to transform the region into South Asia premier deep tech hub. The initiative, led by Chief Minister Nara Chandrababu Naidu and supported by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, moves beyond importing foreign supercomputers to establish a self-sustaining hardware ecosystem and build quantum computers locally from the ground up.
articles.description: The first major test vision of building an indigenous premier deep tech hub arrives soon as an IBM Quantum System, already en route from the U.S., will be installed on February 3, 2027, at Amaravati Quantum Valley; homegrown breakthroughs are already emerging from Amaravati 1Q and Amaravati 1S labs, led by Q SHIVA and NAADA

articles.headline: Child sexual abuse: When boys’ voices break
articles.title: Child sexual abuse: When boys’ voices break
articles.description: Child sexual abuse of boys often goes unreported due to fear, shame, and stigma. Abhinay Deshpande reports from Telangana on families struggling to help their children recover and seek delayed justice

articles.headline: Federal Aviation Administration lifts nationwide ground stop after telecommunications outage
articles.title: FAA ground stop lifted: Why were US flights grounded, and what’s next?
articles.summary: The United States Federal Aviation Administration lifted a nationwide ground stop on Friday after a telecommunications outage overloaded switches and routers at air traffic control centres. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy stated that airspace reopened after four hours of disruption, which cancelled thousands of flights, stranded passengers, and prompted calls for significant air traffic control system upgrades.
articles.description: The FAA says nationwide ground stop disrupting thousands of US flights was caused by a telecommunications outage.

articles.headline: Modi travels to Manila for annual India-ASEAN summit
articles.title: Modi to visit Manila for ASEAN Summit; maritime security, trade on agenda
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will travel to Manila on November 16, 2026, for a three-day visit to attend the annual India-ASEAN summit and the East Asia Summit. Hosted by the Philippines as the current Association of Southeast Asian Nations chair, the meetings will focus on maritime security cooperation and trade and investment ties. Rudrendra Tandon, Secretary in the External Affairs Ministry, confirmed the schedule during a media briefing.
articles.description: Modi is also set to join Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, U.S. President Donald Trump, and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi for the annual Quad summit in Manila. There is, however, no official word on the Quad summit.

articles.headline: U.S. senators order Elon Musk to preserve records on Ukraine Starlink access
articles.title: Democratic U.S. senators order Musk to preserve records on Ukraine Starlink access
articles.summary: Democratic United States senators Jeanne Shaheen and Chris Coons instructed Elon Musk to preserve records regarding SpaceX satellite service restrictions in Ukraine. Ukrainian officials reported disruptions affecting military operations and drone communications. Lawmakers demanded written confirmation by November 30 and requested internal communications dating back to September 1 to address national security concerns involving critical infrastructure.
articles.description: Ukrainian forces say Starshield, the military-grade version of Starlink, is vital for frontline communications and ‌drone operations in their defense against Russian drone and missile attacks

articles.headline: India retail inflation hits 6.1% in October 2026
articles.title: Retail inflation crosses RBI’s upper limit for first time in two years, comes in at 6.1% in October 2026
articles.summary: Retail inflation reached 6.1% in October 2026, exceeding the Reserve Bank of India's upper threshold for the first time in two years. Government data indicates price increases across food, fuel, and services. Economists suggest rising consumer demand and supply-side pressures may prompt the Monetary Policy Committee to implement a 25-basis-point repo rate hike in December.
articles.description: The Consumer Price Index saw almost all categories hit series highs as inflation spread across sectors of the economy

articles.headline: Medical charity warns millions of Ebola funds missing
articles.title: Millions of Ebola dollars missing with staff unpaid while virus spreads, charity says
articles.summary: MÃ©decins Sans FrontiÃ¨res warned that hundreds of millions of dollars allocated for tackling Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo are failing to reach frontline workers, leaving them unpaid and without essential supplies. The outbreak has caused over 5,400 deaths and 11,000 infections since May. The charity urged the Congolese government and United Nations agencies to strengthen accountability while outbreaks spread to neighbouring countries including Kenya, Uganda, and Nigeria.
articles.description: Medical staff are going unpaid, lack proper training and are struggling with shortages of essential supplies, MSF warns

articles.headline: Nvidia launches investigation into Chief Executive Jensen Huang following spy allegations
