articles.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has resigned. What happens next?
articles.summary: Nvidia announced an internal investigation into Chief Executive Jensen Huang after he acknowledged a romantic relationship with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang. United States intelligence reports previously identified Alice Huang as a spy for China's Ministry of State Security. Both Nvidia and Jensen Huang stated they have no reason to believe national security secrets were compromised during the affair.
articles.description: After the leather-jacketed CEO, president, and co-founder of Nvidia, Jensen Huang, acknowledged an affair with Megaspeed exec Alice Huang, his company initially announced an investigation. However, The New York Times reported on Wednesday that there was evidence of another affair, this time with an Nvidia executive who reported directly to him. A board meeting that […]

articles.headline: Nvidia board evaluates potential permanent successors following Jensen Huang departure
articles.title: Who could replace Jensen Huang as Nvidia's permanent chief executive?
articles.summary: Nvidia is evaluating potential internal and external candidates to succeed Jensen Huang as permanent chief executive after his resignation on Thursday, November 12, 2026. Chief financial officer Colette Kress is serving as interim leader while industry experts suggest alternative figures including co-founder Chris Malachowsky, engineering head Ian Buck, and external executives. The leadership transition addresses corporate governance challenges and national security concerns surrounding the artificial intelligence semiconductor supplier.
articles.description: Chief financial officer Colette Kress will replace him temporarily, but several others are in the frame as potential successors.

articles.headline: Trump travels to China for APEC summit amid Nvidia scrutiny
articles.title: Trump heads to China amid Nvidia scandal: Will he get tougher on Beijing?
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump travels to Shenzhen next week for the APEC summit to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping. The visit follows Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang stepping down amid allegations regarding a former Megaspeed executive suspected of working for Chinese intelligence. While Beijing denied the claims, analysts expect trade and export restrictions to remain the primary source of bilateral tension.
articles.description: Outgoing Nvidia chief credited with easing US-China chip ties but personal scandal unlikely to upend next week's talks.

articles.headline: Congress launches website to help voters check electoral roll deletions
articles.title: Congress launches website to help voters check SIR deletions, seek restoration
articles.summary: The Congress party launched a new website on November 13, 2026, enabling citizens to verify if their names were removed from electoral rolls during the special intensive revision and apply for restoration. Congress general secretary K.C. Venugopal announced the platform during the Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao campaign. Party workers will visit polling booths as Vote Rakshaks, and village-level meetings will be organized across India by December 15 to address alleged electoral irregularities.
articles.description: Announcing the initiative, Congress general secretary (organisation) K.C. Venugopal said the website, Iamvoterakshak.in, would allow citizens to verify their names and formally protest against deletions by applying for restoration

articles.headline: Measles-associated deaths reach ten in the United States after two new fatalities
articles.title: Measles-associated deaths reach 10 in US after two more deaths reported
articles.summary: Pennsylvania and Wisconsin announced new measles-associated fatalities, bringing the United States total to ten deaths this year alongside more than 5,400 confirmed cases. A federal dispute emerged between state officials and United States Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. regarding how fatalities are classified. Infectious disease experts warn the ongoing outbreak threatens the nation's measles elimination status achieved in 2000.
articles.description: More than 5,400 confirmed measles cases have been recorded in the US to date this year.

articles.headline: Iran remains open to ceasefire and strait reopening deal
articles.title: ‘No war, no peace’: Can Iran break the deadlock with the US?
articles.summary: Iranian parliament speaker and chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf stated that Tehran remains open to a ceasefire and reopening the Strait of Hormuz through a Qatari mediator. Speaking to Al Jazeera, Ghalibaf said Washington must respond to Tehran's seven conditions, which include sanctions relief and lifting the US naval blockade. Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump reported momentum toward ending the conflict, while Secretary of State Marco Rubio dismissed Iranian demands.
articles.description: Sustainable stalemate or slow-motion strangulation? The current 'equilibrium' is inherently unstable, experts say.

articles.headline: Gaza doctor killed in Israeli strike on Nasser hospital
articles.title: ‘Horrific crime’: Gaza doctor killed as Israel expands war on healthcare
articles.summary: Dr Rizq Abu Shuaira was killed alongside at least five others during an Israeli strike on the surgery department of the Nasser Medical Complex in southern Gaza on Thursday. Zaher al-Waheidi, spokesperson for the Ministry of Health in Gaza, condemned the attack as a horrific crime. The strike caused widespread destruction within the facility, which serves at least 500,000 people, compounding a severe healthcare crisis across the Palestinian territories.
articles.description: Israel's military campaign and mass detentions collapse Palestinian healthcare in Gaza and the West Bank.

articles.headline: Himachal Pradesh cabinet approves monthly financial assistance for women
articles.title: Himachal approves ₹1,500 monthly financial assistance for women
articles.summary: The Himachal Pradesh government approved the Mukhya Mantri Apna Parivar Sukhi Parivar Yojna on November 13, 2026, to provide ₹1,500 monthly to eligible women aged 18 to 59. Chaired by Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu in Shimla, the state cabinet decided that beneficiary families will also receive 300 units of free electricity. The initiative aims to fulfill a key pre-poll promise made by the Congress party during the 2022 Assembly election.
articles.description: Under the scheme, eligible beneficiary families will also receive 300 units of free electricity

articles.headline: 'We'll get home one day' - US travellers impacted by nationwide ground stop
articles.title: 'We'll get home one day' - US travellers impacted by nationwide ground stop
articles.description: Passengers throughout the country were impacted over what the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) describes as “safety and communication issues”.

articles.headline: India and Bangladesh to reschedule fifth round of consular dialogue
articles.title: India-Bangladesh consular dialogue will be held on a mutually convenient date, says Ministry of External Affairs
articles.summary: The Ministry of External Affairs announced on November 13, 2026, that the fifth round of the India-Bangladesh consular dialogue will occur on a mutually convenient date. Spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal stated that India seeks positive bilateral relations through existing mechanisms, including technical discussions on travel arrangements. The talks were postponed following diplomatic tensions surrounding the planned December return to Dhaka of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina.
articles.description: Diplomatic sources had indicated that the postponement of talks was because of the spike in tensions in view of the proposed return of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina to Bangladesh

articles.headline: Tanker collision leaves riverboat passengers clinging to railings
articles.title: Tanker collision leaves riverboat passengers clinging to railings
articles.description: Passengers were rescued after a tanker ship collided with a riverboat docked on the Mississippi River in New Orleans.

articles.headline: Singapore firm Megaspeed emerges as central player in global chip trade
articles.title: Megaspeed: Gaming company to chips linchpin
articles.summary: Singapore-based business Megaspeed, founded in 2023 by Chinese tech executive Alice Huang without prior semiconductor industry experience, rapidly became a crucial intermediary in the Asian chip trade. The firm purchased billions of dollars of technology from artificial intelligence chip manufacturer Nvidia Corporation, drawing intense scrutiny during the recent scandal that resulted in chief executive officer Jensen Huang stepping down.
articles.description: How Megaspeed, a little-known firm started by Alice Huang, became a linchpin in the chips trade

articles.headline: Former FAA official says ‘nobody really knows what is going on’
articles.title: Former FAA official says ‘nobody really knows what is going on’
articles.description: Former FAA safety team representative Kyle Bailey says grounding flights is the safest course of action.

articles.headline: Ukraine faces rolling power cuts amid intensified Russian strikes
articles.title: 'We've got to run': Inside ruined Ukraine power plant under constant drone threat
articles.summary: Ukrainians are enduring planned power outages as Russian forces intensify attacks on the national energy grid. With some families experiencing up to 20 hours without electricity, officials warn that current conditions are becoming unsustainable. Repair efforts at damaged power plants remain difficult due to constant air raids while peace talks between Ukraine and Russia continue.
articles.description: Dan Johnson visits one of the country's largest power stations, barely left standing after a ballistic missile strike by Russia.

articles.headline: Democrat Scott Colom secures historic Senate victory in Mississippi
articles.title: Democrat Scott Colom makes history as Mississippi's first black senator since 19th Century
articles.summary: Democrat Scott Colom narrowly defeated incumbent Republican Cindy Hyde-Smith to win a United States Senate seat in Mississippi. This outcome makes him the state's first Black senator in over 140 years and expands the Democratic majority to fifty-five seats. Colom capitalized on public frustrations regarding economic issues and administration tariffs during a closely watched midterm contest.
articles.description: In a state Trump won two years ago by 22 points, Colom's victory extends a string of Democratic wins in the Senate.

articles.headline: European leaders assess US foreign policy after midterm elections
articles.title: Europe views US with ‘much less horror’ after Trump’s midterms defeat
articles.summary: Following the Democratic Party's victory in the US midterm elections, European experts anticipate limited shifts in transatlantic relations. While a friendlier Congress may emerge, analysts note that President Donald Trump retains significant authority over foreign policy. Concerns persist regarding potential unilateral decisions on Ukraine, trade tariffs, and the ongoing security footprint of US military forces.
articles.description: But experts say Washington’s shift away from Europe runs deeper than Trump and is unlikely to be reversed.

articles.headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang faces board scrutiny over personal scandals
articles.title: Watch: The latest in the Jensen Huang Nvidia scandal
articles.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is under pressure after admitting to an extramarital affair, with reports later revealing a second relationship with a company executive. The board is currently evaluating whether to remove the founder from his position. The BBC reports that the company's leadership is facing significant turmoil as the board considers its next steps.
articles.description: The BBC's China correspondent Laura Bicker explains the timeline of events and what's next for Nvidia as its board considers whether to oust the CEO.

articles.headline: Enforcement Directorate arrests Mahadev betting app co-owner Saurabh Chandrakar
articles.title: After CBI, ED arrests Mahadev betting app scam accused
articles.summary: The Directorate of Enforcement arrested Saurabh Chandrakar, co-owner of the illegal Mahadev Online Book betting syndicate, on Friday, November 13, 2026. A special court in Raipur subsequently remanded him to custody until November 19. According to investigators, Chandrakar and co-promoter Ravi Uppal operated the betting network from Dubai, generating massive earnings through franchise panels and laundering money via hawala channels.
articles.description: “In ED custody, Saurabh Chandrakar will be confronted with the statements of his associates, digital data and documents concerning his foreign entities and evidence of commission of offence of money laundering,” an ED official said

articles.headline: London police open sex offence investigation into comedian David Walliams
articles.title: UK police open sex offence probe into comedian and author David Walliams
articles.summary: The Metropolitan Police in London launched an investigation into non-recent serious sexual offences involving British comedian and author David Walliams following media reports accusing him of grooming and abuse. Walliams, who is 55 years old and denies all allegations, has been dropped by his literary agency and had several shows removed by the BBC. The probe follows investigative reports published by ITV News and The Guardian.
articles.description: The British TV personality, 55, denies sexual assault allegations, saying he has not broken the law.

articles.headline: Afghanistan completes a road to the Chinese border despite closure
articles.title: Afghanistan’s new road to China ends at a closed border
articles.summary: Afghanistan completed an unpaved road through the Wakhan Corridor to the Chinese border in Badakhshan province. Funded by the Afghan government at a cost of 365 million afghanis, the project aims to boost trade. However, Beijing has not opened the border or commented on the route, as China prioritizes strict regional security guarantees over commercial access due to ongoing threat concerns.
articles.description: Taliban government hopes its Wakhan Corridor road will open new trade routes and reduce reliance on Pakistan.

articles.headline: Ugandan army arrests senior generals amid presidential succession political tensions
articles.title: Arrested generals and a threatened VP: President's son fuels Ugandan succession fever
articles.summary: The Ugandan military detained at least a dozen senior officers during a crackdown led by army commander General Muhoozi Kainerugaba. The arrests, which include former intelligence chiefs, coincide with political divisions over the presidential succession of long-ruling President Yoweri Museveni. While officials defended the actions as anti-corruption measures, analysts argue the moves target officers opposing the general's ambitions.
articles.description: The 52-year-old general’s provocative posts and military threats have fuelled rumours of a dynastic succession.

articles.headline: Nvidia board considers removal of CEO Jensen Huang
articles.title: Nvidia board weighs Jensen Huang’s future: Can it remove its founder?
articles.summary: Nvidia's board is weighing the removal of CEO Jensen Huang following reports of extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected of spying for China. The company has lost over $600 billion in market value this week. While the board investigates potential foreign intelligence links, Huang faces a November 18 briefing request from US House committee chairs.
articles.description: CEO of chip maker is under scrutiny after reports of affairs, including a relationship with an alleged Chinese spy.

articles.headline: Iran Revolutionary Guards report tanker explosions in Strait of Hormuz
articles.title: Iran’s Guards say ‘accident’ left two tankers on fire in Hormuz
articles.summary: According to the Iranian Revolutionary Guards, two oil supertankers carrying over four million barrels caught fire following an accident on an unauthorized Strait of Hormuz route. Tehran blamed aggressive American military policies for the incident on November 12, 2026. The route was restricted amid ongoing West Asian conflict, while U.S. forces maintained a naval blockade and denied active mine threats.
articles.description: Iranian forces have made multiple announcements in recent weeks of ships catching fire attempting to use routes that Tehran considers off-limits

articles.headline: Manchester United dismiss manager Michael Carrick following club's worst start
articles.title: Michael Carrick sacked as Manchester United manager after club’s worst start to a Premier League season
articles.summary: Manchester United dismissed manager Michael Carrick on November 12, 2026, following a disappointing 4-4 draw against Aston Villa that placed the English club in the relegation zone at 18th place. The twenty-time English champion secured only one league victory and eight points from ten matches, prompting leadership to seek a permanent successor. Mauricio Pochettino has emerged as a potential replacement.
articles.description: Manchester United are linked with a move to sign U.S. men’s coach Mauricio Pochettino to replace Carrick

articles.headline: Singapore investigates data firm linked to Nvidia chip export scandal
articles.title: How the Jensen Huang scandal created a headache for business-friendly Singapore
articles.summary: Singapore authorities are investigating Megaspeed, a data centre company, over suspected fraudulent declarations regarding the export of high-end Nvidia chips. The probe follows concerns that the firm bypassed US export controls to supply Chinese companies. Nvidia founder Jensen Huang recently resigned following an affair with the former head of Megaspeed, Alice Huang, amid ongoing international scrutiny.
articles.description: The scandal has cast a spotlight on Singapore's success as a chip hub - and a location for alleged illicit trade.

articles.headline: China urges US to stop fabricating spy claims regarding Nvidia CEO
articles.title: China says US ‘fabricating’ Nvidia spy claims to justify tech ‘blockade’
articles.summary: Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning stated that allegations linking Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang to a Chinese intelligence agent are baseless pretexts for a technological blockade. The remarks follow an internal company investigation into Huang and precede an upcoming meeting between United States President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen.
articles.description: Nvidia CEO is under investigation for an affair with a woman whom US intelligence believes to be a Chinese spy.

articles.headline: Rescue operations underway after tanker strikes cruise boat in New Orleans
articles.title: 32 passengers taken to hospital after tanker hits river cruise boat in US
articles.summary: A tanker collided with the American Heritage river cruise boat on the Mississippi River in New Orleans on Friday, causing the vessel to partially submerge. Emergency responders are currently conducting search-and-rescue operations for the 129 passengers on board. The cause of the collision remains unknown as authorities work to evacuate all guests and crew members.
articles.description: American Heritage paddleboat with 129 passengers on board is partially submerged on Mississippi River in New Orleans.

articles.headline: New York building collapse leaves two dead and seventeen injured
articles.title: New York building collapse kills at least two, officials say
articles.summary: At least two individuals died and over seventeen sustained injuries after a three-storey structure in Brooklyn collapsed into an open construction site on Wednesday. Over two hundred and fifty first responders deployed to the Flatbush Avenue location for rescue operations. Authorities stated the cause remains undetermined while emergency crews continued searching through rubble for survivors trapped beneath the debris.
articles.description: A dangerous search for survivors continues after a three-storey building collapsed in Brooklyn on Wednesday afternoon.

articles.headline: Indonesian vice president steps down following educational credential disputes
articles.title: Indonesia's Vice President resigns as eligibility and academic credentials are questioned
articles.summary: Gibran Rakabuming Raka resigned as Indonesia's vice president on November 12, 2026, following Supreme Court and Constitutional Court rulings regarding his overseas education documents. The thirty-nine-year-old submitted his resignation to the People's Consultative Assembly in Jakarta after one hundred twenty lawmakers filed a petition initiating parliamentary procedures that could have led to his impeachment.
articles.description: The Constitutional Court and the Supreme Court ruled last month that the documents submitted by Gibran Rakabuming Raka, the 39-year-old son of former President Joko Widodo, regarding his overseas education didn't meet election requirements

articles.headline: US military bases become strategic liabilities following Middle East conflict
articles.title: From the UK to the Gulf, are US overseas bases becoming liabilities?
articles.summary: Recent military engagements in the Middle East have transformed critical overseas US installations into potential liabilities for Washington and its allies. Facilities in the United Kingdom and Gulf nations suffered damage during the war, prompting the relocation of assets and raising concerns among host governments regarding increased security risks from regional adversaries.
articles.description: For decades, these bases allowed the US to wage faraway wars. Now, Iran has changed that calculation.

articles.headline: Xi Jinping calls for complete reunification of Taiwan during commemorative speech
articles.title: Xi says Taiwan 'reunification' must happen as history cannot be stopped
articles.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping stated on November 12, 2026, that the reunification of Taiwan is an unwavering historical mission that must be realized. Speaking in Beijing during an event honoring Sun Yat-sen, Xi emphasized peaceful development under the one-China principle while maintaining that the tide of history cannot be stopped despite strong Taiwanese opposition.
articles.description: China views democratically governed Taiwan as its own territory, despite Taipei's strong rejection of that claim, and has repeatedly offered a "one country, two systems" model of autonomy

articles.headline: Watch: Cruise ship seen sinking after collision with cargo ship in New Orleans
articles.title: Watch: Cruise ship seen sinking after collision with cargo ship in New Orleans
articles.description: All passengers have been accounted for after a cargo ship collided with a docked cruise ship.

articles.headline: Chinese AI firms rush to secure foreign Nvidia chip capacity
articles.title: Chinese AI firms rush to secure Nvidia chip capacity as spy scandal stirs fear of U.S. curbs
articles.summary: Chinese artificial intelligence companies are seeking to rent Nvidia-powered computing capacity at overseas data centres amid fears that a scandal involving the chipmaker's chief executive Jensen Huang could prompt Washington to tighten restrictions. Sources indicated that buyers are stockpiling restricted processors over concerns that U.S. authorities might crack down further on cross-border technology smuggling.
articles.description: A major Chinese ‌cloud provider has discussed internally whether to lock in overseas Nvidia chip capacity, while some companies have ‌contacted ⁠data-centre operators about reserving it, per sources

articles.headline: Deepti Sharma named ICC Women’s Player of the Month for October
articles.title: Deepti Sharma named ICC Women’s Player of the Month for October
articles.summary: Indian all-rounder Deepti Sharma received the International Cricket Council Women's Player of the Month award for October. The 29-year-old earned the honour after scoring 155 runs and taking seven wickets during India's undefeated series against Zimbabwe. Meanwhile, South African all-rounder Marco Jansen was selected as the ICC Men's Player of the Month for his performance.
articles.description: Deepti Sharma beat Bangladesh’s Sobhana Mostary and Australia’s Annabel Sutherland to claim the monthly honour

articles.headline: US envoys arrive in Moscow for high-level peace talks with Putin
articles.title: US envoys meet Putin in Moscow to discuss Russia-Ukraine war
articles.summary: United States envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff travelled to Moscow on Thursday for discussions with Russian President Vladimir Putin. The visit followed trilateral peace negotiations in Abu Dhabi that concluded on Wednesday without a breakthrough on the nearly five-year war, though participants discussed post-war security guarantees and upcoming prisoner exchanges.
articles.description: The meeting with Kushner and Witkoff comes after two days of trilateral talks in the UAE yielded no breakthrough.

articles.headline: Pakistani influencer linked to terror investigations across fourteen Indian states
articles.title: The digital recruiter | Shahzad Bhatti
articles.summary: Over the past two years, Pakistani social-media influencer Shahzad Bhatti has been implicated in multiple Indian anti-terror investigations spanning 14 states. Authorities reported that young men allegedly acting on his instructions were arrested under the Unlawful Activities Prevention Act for tasks including hanging promotional posters, installing live-streamed CCTVs, and making extortion calls.
articles.description: The Pakistani social media influencer’s campaign to establish fear and clout in India has spread to 14 States, leading the Home Ministry to designate his network as a terror group

articles.headline: Pope Leo cheered on return to Peru city where he served as bishop
articles.title: Pope Leo cheered on return to Peru city where he served as bishop
articles.description: An estimated 1.5 million people have welcomed Pope Leo XIV back to the city in Peru where he once served as bishop.

articles.headline: Indonesian Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka submits resignation letter
articles.title: Indonesia's vice-president resigns amid signs ruling alliance is fraying
articles.summary: Indonesian Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka tendered his resignation to President Prabowo Subianto after the Supreme Court invalidated a high-school document used in his 2024 election campaign. The ruling sparked parliamentary impeachment initiatives and highlighted widening fractures within the ruling political alliance established by former leader Joko Widodo.
articles.description: The news comes at a turbulent time for President Prabowo, who faces a growing rift with his predecessor Joko Widodo.

articles.headline: India exempts rules to purchase Israeli phone-hacking and surveillance technology
articles.title: India bypasses own rules to buy Israeli phone-hacking tech
articles.summary: India exempted an Israeli firm from procurement regulations, allowing government agencies to purchase phone-extraction and surveillance technology. Documents reviewed by digital-rights groups revealed Home Minister Amit Shah approved waivers for forensic equipment, enabling security forces to access cloud data and bypass security locks despite privacy concerns raised by legal experts.
articles.description: India's expansive surveillance capabilities extend beyond cloning phones to accessing cloud-based data of tech giants.

articles.headline: Gunmen kill ten police officers and eighteen fighters in Pakistan
articles.title: Ten police officers, 18 fighters killed in northwest Pakistan attack
articles.summary: Ten police officers and 18 fighters died during violence in northwestern Pakistan after armed men attacked officers returning from an illegal gold mining operation in the Kohat district. The Pakistani Taliban claimed responsibility for the assault, which also left 12 police personnel wounded as security forces continue battling intensifying regional unrest.
articles.description: Officers were returning from a mine in Kohat district when fighters opened fire on them, authorities say.

articles.headline: Xi Jinping says Taiwan ‘reunification’ with China must happen
articles.title: Xi Jinping says Taiwan ‘reunification’ with China must happen
articles.description: Xi Jinping, President of China, has called for the peaceful ‘reunification’ of Taiwan with China.

articles.headline: Pope Leo returns to former diocese in Peru following cancer surgery
articles.title: Pope thanks crowds on emotional return to ‘second home’ in Peru’s Chiclayo
articles.summary: Pope Leo visited Chiclayo in Peru on Wednesday to thank supporters one month after undergoing lung cancer surgery. About 500,000 people attended Mass at Pampas de Pimentel, while a million lined the motorcade route. The Chicago-born pontiff, formerly known as Robert Francis Prevost, served as bishop there from 2015 to 2023. His 12-day South American tour concludes on Sunday after previous stops in Argentina and Uruguay.
articles.description: The Chicago-born pope was welcomed by huge crowds in the coastal city, on the final leg of his South America tour.

articles.headline: Gautam Gambhir expresses concern over batting collapses ahead of World Cup
articles.title: Gambhir concerned about India's batting collapses ahead of World Cup
articles.summary: India head coach Gautam Gambhir stated on Friday that he is worried about rapid batting collapses after his team was bowled out for 89 by New Zealand in the fourth ODI in South Africa. The heavy 244-run defeat follows a previous match where India struggled to chase 135. Gambhir highlighted challenges posed by New Zealand pacers Matt Henry and Kyle Jamieson, noting that dropped catches also contributed to the loss.
articles.description: “You’re always concerned when you get bundled out for 90-odd. Why won’t I be concerned? These are conditions which are going to be closest to what we might get during the World Cup,” Gambhir said

articles.headline: Paraguayan prosecutors file new criminal association charge against Santiago Pena
articles.title: Paraguay’s ex-president Pena faces new charge over Ueno bank collapse
articles.summary: Paraguayan prosecutors charged former president Santiago Pena with criminal association on Friday regarding the collapse of the digital bank Ueno. The 47-year-old politician, currently held in pretrial detention after being impeached last week, is accused of directing state funds to the firm. Investigators raided his official residence in Asuncion on Thursday, while three former central bank officials were also arrested.
articles.description: The criminal association charge over his alleged role in the collapse of the bank comes a week after his removal.

articles.headline: Nigeria completes 21-day Ebola contact monitoring period with zero infections
articles.title: Nigeria ends 21-day Ebola contact monitoring with no secondary transmission
articles.summary: The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention announced on Friday that 62 contacts of a recent Ebola patient completed a 21-day monitoring period without falling ill. The index case involved a Swiss woman who travelled to Uganda and Nigeria before being evacuated to Switzerland, where she fully recovered. Authorities noted that an official end to the outbreak requires a 42-day countdown under World Health Organization protocols.
articles.description: None of the 62 contacts identified after the first case developed the disease, although 13 contacts reported fever.

articles.headline: Scott Bessent blames Commerce Department for failing to oversee Nvidia chip exports
articles.title: Nvidia scandal fallout widens as Trump's treasury secretary blames cabinet colleague
articles.summary: United States Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent criticized the Commerce Department led by Howard Lutnick for failing to properly oversee high-specification Nvidia chip exports. The controversy follows the ousting of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy whose firm faced smuggling investigations.
articles.description: Scott Bessent suggests Howard Lutnick’s commerce department failed to ban exports of Nvidia's chips to a firm thought to have links with China.

articles.headline: Clint Eastwood directed the sports film Invictus about Nelson Mandela
articles.title: Invictus again: South Africa’s cinematic rise to the Test summit
articles.summary: The cinematic film Invictus portrays how South African President Nelson Mandela utilized the 1995 Rugby World Cup to unite the nation following the end of apartheid. Directed by Clint Eastwood, the movie stars Morgan Freeman as Mandela and Matt Damon as Springboks captain Francois Pienaar, highlighting how sport served as a crucial tool for national reconciliation during a pivotal historical period.
articles.description: The Proteas, under Temba Bavuma and Shukri Conrad, hold both the World Test Championship and the No. 1 ranking — a position of affairs that seemed unimaginable in 2024 when a second-string side, a compromise because of the SA20’s emergence, was thrashed by New Zealand.

articles.headline: National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority warns manufacturers over anti-cancer drug prices
articles.title: Comply with new prices of 137 anti-cancer drugs or face action, says regulator
articles.summary: The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority warned on Friday that manufacturers must comply with revised prices for 137 non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs or face penal action. The price caps, which limit trade margins to 30 percent, took effect on November 9 following an October 17 gazette order. State drug controllers were instructed to monitor compliance across the supply chain and submit action reports by November 16.
articles.description: NPPA directs State drug controllers to strictly monitor prices

articles.headline: Iran open to deal if US ‘refrains from excessive demands’, says Ghalibaf
articles.title: Iran open to deal if US ‘refrains from excessive demands’, says Ghalibaf
articles.description: Iran’s chief negotiator says Iran is open to a deal if the US refrains from creating distrust and excessive demands.

articles.headline: Migrants risk deadly route to Spain’s Canary Islands
articles.title: Migrants risk deadly route to Spain’s Canary Islands
articles.description: More than 7,400 migrants arrived in Spain’s Canary Islands during the first 10 days of November.

articles.headline: G7 Foreign Ministers warn China's actions east of Taiwan threaten stability
articles.title: G7 Foreign Ministers say China's actions east of Taiwan threaten stability
articles.summary: Group of Seven Foreign Ministers issued a joint declaration in Paris late Wednesday stating that China's assertive maritime activities east of Taiwan threaten regional stability and freedom of navigation. Taiwan views the increased coast guard patrols as preparation for a potential blockade, while China claims sovereignty over the democratically governed island.
articles.description: The G7 statement said the Ministers ⁠stressed the importance of maintaining peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait

articles.headline: Bengaluru metro opens Pink Line elevated section amid mixed commuter reactions
articles.title: Bengaluru Pink Line begins operations today; BMRCL announces timings as commuters seek faster completion of underground section
articles.summary: The Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited launched train services on an elevated section between Kalena Agrahara and S.G. Palya following inauguration by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Commuters expressed mixed views regarding limited connectivity benefits while awaiting the underground section. Fares range from ten to thirty rupees, and the Bengaluru Metropolitan Transport Corporation introduced five dedicated feeder bus routes starting November 14 to enhance local transport integration.

articles.headline: T.N. Governor meets Home Minister Amit Shah in New Delhi
articles.title: T.N. Governor meets Home Minister Amit Shah in New Delhi

articles.headline: Senator Chris Van Hollen challenges Chuck Schumer for Democratic leadership
articles.title: Democratic Senate leader Schumer set to face leadership challenge
articles.summary: United States Senator Chris Van Hollen announced a leadership challenge against Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer as Democrats prepare to control Congress following midterm elections. Van Hollen argued the party needs new leadership to address working-class concerns. Senator Schumer welcomed discussion while affirming his intention to continue leading his caucus in the Senate.
articles.description: Maryland Senator Van Hollen says "new leadership" is needed for Democrats following the party's recent midterm successes.

articles.headline: Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang resigns and faces congressional testimony
articles.title: How will the US deal with Nvidia scandal?
articles.summary: The technology company leader stepped down from his position and is scheduled to address the United States Congress after acknowledging a personal relationship with a woman alleged to have connections to Chinese intelligence. Federal authorities including the Federal Bureau of Investigation and the Department of Justice initiated inquiries, although corporate representatives stated that enterprise information and national security remained uncompromised during the incident.
articles.description: Tech giant CEO resigned and will testify before Congress.

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu inflation rate criticized by PMK president
articles.title: Take steps to control inflation, Anbumani Ramadoss tells State govt.
articles.summary: Pattali Makkal Katchi president Anbumani Ramadoss criticized the Tamil Nadu state government on Friday for recording India's highest inflation rate at 7.29% in October. According to union government statistics, rising prices of essential food items like rice and pulses have severely impacted poor and middle-class families, while per capita income has declined across the state.
articles.description: Poor and middle class families are facing severe hardship due to rising prices of essential food commodities, including rice, pulses and edible oils, says PMK leader

articles.headline: Israeli airstrike on Nasser Hospital building in Khan Younis kills five
articles.title: Israeli strike on southern Gaza hospital kills six, health authorities say
articles.summary: An Israeli airstrike hit the surgery department at Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis on Thursday, killing at least five people including a surgeon named Rezik Abushira and wounding twenty others, according to the civil defence service. The strike caused extensive damage to the facility. This event occurs amid ongoing conflict and mounting casualties across the Gaza Strip since the October 2023 offensive began.
articles.description: Israeli forces have previously targeted Nasser Hospital; in 2025, the military killed five journalists — including AP contributor Mariam Dagga — when it struck a gathering point for local reporters at the complex

articles.headline: Benjamin Netanyahu urges national unity government during contentious Israeli parliament session
articles.title: Netanyahu’s legacy: Personality politics reshapes Israeli democracy
articles.summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called for a national unity government during the swearing-in of the Israeli parliament, the Knesset, on Tuesday. The session featured intense heckling and walkouts as political rivals opposed his leadership. Gadi Eisenkot, tasked with forming a new administration, cancelled coalition talks and declared Netanyahu unfit for office amid ongoing corruption trials and political polarization.
articles.description: Netanyahu's fight for political survival turns the parliament's opening into a scene of insults and acrimony.

articles.headline: Ten killed in Guinea during gold mining enforcement clashes
articles.title: At least 10 killed in Guinea clashes over gold mining ban
articles.summary: At least 10 people died and 13 others sustained injuries during clashes between protesters and security forces in Balato, Guinea, on Wednesday. The Ministry of Territorial Administration stated that the violence erupted when security forces enforced a November 2 ban on artisanal gold mining aimed at curbing severe environmental damage caused by unregulated extraction.
articles.description: Guinea banned artisanal gold mining in Siguiri on November 2 due to environmental degradation, causing mass exodus.

articles.headline: Indonesian vice president resigns amid credential dispute and political pressure
articles.title: Indonesia vice president resigns amid dispute over eligibility
articles.summary: Indonesian Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka resigned on Thursday after court rulings disputed his educational credentials, according to parliamentary officials. The thirty-nine-year-old official stepped down during a period of widespread public protests regarding economic hardship and corruption, leaving the People's Consultative Assembly sixty days to elect a presidential nominee as his replacement.
articles.description: Gibran Rakabuming Raka, son of former President Joko Widodo, resigns as court questions his overseas education.

articles.headline: Germany ready to discuss critical mineral partnerships with India
articles.title: Germany open to discussing critical mineral partnerships with India, says Ambassador
articles.summary: German Ambassador to India Jasper Wieck stated on Friday that Germany is open to enhancing critical mineral cooperation and supporting India in recycling industrial waste. Speaking in Coimbatore, Ambassador Wieck emphasized that both nations face shortages of critical minerals and highlighted Germany's ongoing willingness to share vocational training expertise.

articles.headline: Low pressure area forms over Bay of Bengal
articles.title: Low pressure area forms over Bay of Bengal, likely to intensify into cyclonic storm around November 16
articles.summary: A low-pressure system formed over the Southeast Bay of Bengal on Friday and is expected to intensify into a cyclonic storm by the evening of November 16, according to the India Meteorological Department. Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority Managing Director Prakhar Jain warned fishermen against venturing into rough seas as authorities monitor the storm track.

articles.headline: Indian Navy conducts coastal defence drills off Visakhapatnam
articles.title: Navy, security agencies hold coastal defence drills off Visakhapatnam
articles.summary: The Indian Navy and various security agencies executed coastal security drills off Visakhapatnam on Friday as part of the fifth edition of Exercise Sea Vigil-26. The operations featured joint patrols, marine commando boarding actions, and three-layered surveillance spanning 3,460 kilometers of coastline across eastern states and union territories under lead agency direction.

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh leads rooftop solar adoption as national capacity expands
articles.title: Andhra Pradesh emerges as a leader in India’s rooftop solar push: Union Minister
articles.summary: Union Minister for New and Renewable Energy Pralhad Joshi announced that India has increased its non-fossil fuel capacity to cover nearly fifty-five percent of total power generation. Speaking at the CII Partnership Summit, he highlighted that Andhra Pradesh has enabled over seven lakh households to install rooftop solar systems. India aims to achieve five hundred gigawatts of non-fossil capacity by the year 2030.
articles.description: Pralhad Joshi says 7.86 lakh households in the State have adopted rooftop solar as India meets peak power demand of 270 GW without interruption; solar capacity rises to 175 GW

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu government imposes stock limits on paddy, rice and pulses
articles.title: Tamil Nadu government imposes stock limits on paddy, rice and pulses; excess stocks must be cleared by November 16
articles.summary: The Tamil Nadu government imposed stock limits on paddy, rice, tur dal, and pulses across the State to prevent hoarding and curb food inflation, according to orders issued on November 14, 2026. Wholesalers and retailers must clear excess stocks by November 16 under the new regulations, which remain in force until early 2027 to ensure fair pricing and equitable distribution.
articles.description: Govt. directs those holding stocks in excess of prescribed quantities to bring them within limits by Nov. 16; the orders will apply throughout the State and come into force with immediate effect

articles.headline: Gadi Eisenkot slams Benjamin Netanyahu over alleged racist election campaign
articles.title: Eisenkot slams Netanyahu’s ‘racist’ campaign against Palestinian Israelis
articles.summary: Israeli prime ministerial hopeful Gadi Eisenkot accused caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of fuelling a racist and violent campaign of delegitimisation against Palestinian citizens of Israel. Writing on X on November 14, 2026, Eisenkot condemned the marginalisation of Arab citizens, who secured 19 seats in the October 27 elections, while noting that he has six weeks to form a new government.
articles.description: Prime ministerial hopeful calls attempts to marginalise and smear Palestinian citizens of Israel 'an anti-state act'.

articles.headline: Passenger detained over bomb hoax on Kolkata Mumbai flight
articles.title: Man held for planting hoax ‘hijack’ threat in Kolkata-Mumbai Air India flight
articles.summary: Authorities apprehended a passenger and handed them over to airport police following a hoax hijack threat aboard an Air India flight from Kolkata to Mumbai. A cabin crew member discovered a handwritten threat note inside the aircraft lavatory before departure, prompting safety checks and deboarding of all 105 passengers. The flight eventually departed several hours later after security procedures declared the threat a hoax.
articles.description: Confessing after his handwriting matched, the man said his wife and he had been ailing from cancer for a long time; he wanted the flight cancelled as he did not wish to leave her

articles.headline: Tata Trusts vice-chairmen reject Darius Khambata criticism over governance
articles.title: Tata feud: Venu Srinivasan, Vijay Singh hit back at Khambata, accuse him of ignoring governance failures
articles.summary: Tata Trusts Vice-Chairmen Venu Srinivasan and Vijay Singh defended the Tata Sons board in a November 11, 2026 letter, responding to criticism from fellow trustee Darius Khambata. The dispute centres on the Reserve Bank of India rejecting the holding company's deregistration application in September 2026, the reappointment of Chairman N. Chandrasekaran, and whether listing Tata Sons threatens the philanthropic trust model.
articles.description: In a five-page letter, the two Vice-Chairmen of Tata Trusts said opposition to listing Tata Sons should not be driven by a wish to keep control in the Trusts’ leadership’s hands

articles.headline: Sunil Bharti Mittal calls for India to retain satellite kill switch control
articles.title: Mittal says India must hold satellite ‘kill switch’, warns against dependence on single provider
articles.summary: Bharti Airtel founder Sunil Bharti Mittal urged India to maintain control over satellite communications kill switches during an interview marking Bharti Enterprises' 50th anniversary. Warning against relying on a single foreign provider, Mittal noted that operators like Eutelsat OneWeb and Starlink await final operational clearances amid broader strategic debates over national security and space infrastructure.
articles.description: Bharti Enterprises chairman Sunil Bharti Mittal says India should not rely on one country or company for satellite communications, as OneWeb, Jio and Starlink await operational clearances

articles.headline: Stock markets snap three-day rally as retail inflation surges
articles.title: Stock markets snap three-day rally on rate hike fears; Sensex drops 318 points
articles.summary: Indian benchmark equity indices declined on November 13, 2026, ending a three-day winning streak due to rising retail inflation expectations. The BSE Sensex fell 318.56 points to close at 81,592.45, while the NSE Nifty dropped 155.05 points to 25,144.30, following data showing October retail inflation surged to 6.09% and breached the central bank target.
articles.description: Retail inflation surged to 6.09% in October, breaching the RBI’s upper tolerance limit for the first time in two years and prompting expectations of a rate hike next month

articles.headline: Nvidia board prepares to oust CEO Jensen Huang following affair revelations
articles.title: Nvidia preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang: U.S. media
articles.summary: The board of directors at chip manufacturer Nvidia is preparing to remove co-founder and Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang. This development follows recent disclosures that the sixty-three-year-old executive had an extramarital affair with an individual accused by United States intelligence of being a Chinese spy, alongside a second relationship with a subordinate at the technology company.
articles.description: The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang was also involved in a second extramarital affair, with Nvidia's vice-president of health care, Kimberly Powell

articles.headline: Syria rescinds entry restrictions for United States travellers
articles.title: Syria removes visa restrictions on U.S. travellers after backlash
articles.summary: Syria reversed a temporary interior ministry directive requiring United States citizens to obtain prior visa authorisation on November 13, 2026, following online complaints. Ports and borders authority official Mazen Allouch confirmed entry procedures returned to previous rules allowing Americans to obtain visas at Damascus airport or border crossings. Tourism has risen following the 2024 government transition.
articles.description: The current Syrian government, in place since Islamist-led fighters overthrew Bashar al-Assad in December 2024, has allowed Westerners to obtain entry visas at Damascus airport or border crossings

articles.headline: Stelco implements temporary layoffs affecting hundreds of Canadian steelworkers
articles.title: The fight over Canadian steelworker jobs
articles.summary: Stelco initiated temporary layoffs affecting hundreds of workers at its Hamilton and Nanticoke plants in Ontario. American owner Cleveland-Cliffs blamed United States tariffs implemented by President Donald Trump and foreign competition. Meanwhile, union representatives and government officials questioned whether the cuts were genuinely necessary or served corporate interests instead.
articles.description: Stelco's US owner blames Trump's tariffs for layoffs, but its support for those same tariffs has raised questions.

articles.headline: Gadi Eisenkot defends Arab minority after Benjamin Netanyahu attacks
articles.title: Eisenkot urges respect for Israel's Arab minority after Netanyahu attacks
articles.summary: Israeli caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu linked Arab lawmakers to Hamas, drawing a rebuke from political hopeful Gadi Eisenkot on November 13, 2026. Two Arab-majority parties won 19 seats in the election. President Isaac Herzog tasked Mr. Eisenkot with forming a government, though right-wing allies object to Arab inclusion.
articles.description: Two Arab-majority parties, Raam and the Joint List, secured a combined 19 seats in last month's election, winning nearly a sixth of the 120-seat parliament and potentially emerging as kingmakers in efforts by Eisenkot to form a government

articles.headline: Ambati Rayudu overhauls Hyderabad cricket systems to boost performance
articles.title: Ploughing through the red tape: Inside Ambati Rayudu’s mission to fix Hyderabad cricket
articles.summary: Hyderabad Cricket Association Director of Cricket Operations Ambati Rayudu has implemented structural reforms, increasing match schedules and revamping pitches at the Gymkhana ground. These efforts have helped Hyderabad top the Elite Group B table with 20 points after winning three matches and drawing one in the Ranji Trophy season.
articles.description: In the six months since Ambati Rayudu promised to change the culture, the former India batter has been spotted pitch-side at dawn, at a soil vendor’s door in the rain and, by his own count, five to seven kilos lighter

articles.headline: Opposition MPs urge wider nationwide consultations on FCRA Bill
articles.title: Opposition members call for FCRA panel to hold wider consultations across country
articles.summary: Opposition members wrote to parliamentary panel chairperson Sanjay Jaiswal on November 12, 2026, requesting broader nationwide consultations regarding the Foreign Contribution Regulation Amendment Bill. The Joint Committee met 25 organisations in one day, hearing opposing views from Christian groups concerned over charitable work and RSS linked entities advocating for stricter foreign funding regulations.
articles.description: Parliamentary panel meets 25 organisations on Thursday, November 12, as it rushes to finalise its report in time for the upcoming Parliament session

articles.headline: Pakistan calls for immediate cessation of Houthi attacks
articles.title: Pakistan calls for 'immediate' end to Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia at UN
articles.summary: Pakistan demanded an immediate and unconditional halt to Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia during a United Nations Security Council session on Thursday, November 12, 2026. Pakistan's Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Ambassador Syed Haider Shah, expressed full solidarity with Saudi Arabia's security, as the council unanimously adopted a resolution renewing targeted sanctions for another year.
articles.description: UN Security Council renewed targeted sanctions under its Yemen sanctions regime for another year

articles.headline: Abhimanyu Mishra draws against Magnus Carlsen in championship
articles.title: Total Chess: Abhimanyu holds his own against Carlsen
articles.summary: American Grandmaster Abhimanyu Mishra drew both of his round-three matches against world number one Magnus Carlsen during the Total Chess World Championship Tour pilot on Thursday, November 13, 2026. The seventeen-year-old secured a balanced Italian Game with black pieces before successfully defending an inferior position in an eighty-move Scandinavian Defence return game.

articles.headline: Nitin Gadkari says world-class roads are vital for India's economic growth
articles.title: CII Summit in Vizag: World-class roads crucial for India’s economic progress, says Gadkari
articles.summary: Union Minister Nitin Gadkari stated that advanced road infrastructure is essential for national economic progress and Andhra Pradesh development during the 31st CII Partnership Summit on November 13, 2026. Highlighting projects like the Surat–Chennai Expressway and Amaravati Outer Ring Road, he noted that the National Highway network in the State expanded significantly between 2014 and 2026, while State Minister B.C. Janardhan Reddy emphasized investment opportunities.
articles.description: Proposed at a cost of ₹32,000 crore, the 195-km Amaravati Outer Ring Road project will soon get the Cabinet’s approval, says the Union Minister

articles.headline: Security forces question suspects following Kulgam CRPF post attack
articles.title: J&K Police zero in on LeT operative, two foreigners in Kulgam CRPF attack
articles.summary: Authorities detained several suspects for questioning following a terrorist attack on a Central Reserve Police Force post in South Kashmir's Kulgam district on November 11, 2026. Security forces intensified cordon and search operations, established vehicle checkpoints, and deployed armoured vehicles across the district by November 13, 2026, to track down the responsible individuals.
articles.description: Lashkar-e-Taiba operative Mohammad Lateef Bha is wanted for two attacks in Anantnag and Kulgam last July that left a police officer and two workers from Chhattisgarh dead

articles.headline: Telangana Women's Commission probes ART centres over illegal oocyte racket
articles.title: Telangana Women’s Commission issues notices to eight ART centres in illegal oocyte racket case
articles.summary: The Telangana State Women's Commission initiated an inquiry into an alleged illegal egg donation racket on November 13, 2026, issuing notices to eight Assisted Reproductive Technology centres. Chairperson Nerella Sharada expressed dissatisfaction with institutional representation and questioned claims that ninety percent of donors were voluntary and unremunerated, prompting discussions on strengthening regulatory oversight with health officials.

articles.headline: SP and Congress say AIMIM-ASP alliance will not impact INDIA bloc
articles.title: No impact on INDIA alliance prospects in view of AIMIM-ASP pact, says Congress-SP
articles.summary: Leaders from the Samajwadi Party and Congress stated on November 13, 2026, that the newly formed Samajik Parivartan Morcha alliance between AIMIM and the Azad Samaj Party will not affect INDIA bloc prospects in upcoming Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. While acknowledging potential minor vote shifts, representatives argued that voters recognize the BJP alternative, following the alliance announcement by Asaduddin Owaisi and Chandrashekhar Azad.
articles.description: Dalits and Muslims at the ground level remain cautious about the intent and viability of this sudden, unnatural alliance, say leaders

articles.headline: Kerala High Court calls lack of KIIFB CAG audit concerning
articles.title: KIIFB accounts should have been audited by CAG, says Kerala High Court
articles.summary: The Kerala High Court observed that the previous State government's failure to subject KIIFB accounts to a Comptroller and Auditor General audit was concerning, noting preliminary discrepancies. The court disposed of a public interest litigation after noting the current government's decision to comprehensively audit the board, which held outstanding loan liabilities amounting to over twenty thousand crore rupees by March 31, 2024.
articles.description: In a public interest litigation, petitioner argues that the guarantees furnished by the State government to KIIFB against borrowings bypassed the limits set by the Centre and created 'off-Budget borrowings' that threatened the State’s fiscal stability and required mandatory CAG oversight

articles.headline: Yemen conflict intensifies as Houthis deny targeting Mecca
articles.title: Fighting intensifies in Yemen as Houthis deny targeting Mecca
articles.summary: Yemeni Houthis rejected Saudi allegations regarding a drone strike on Mecca, claiming instead that strikes targeted Yanbu and Riyadh. Meanwhile, fighting escalated inside Yemen between government forces and Houthi fighters, with total casualties reaching 11,755 according to the World Health Organization. Over 320,000 people have been displaced since August as intensified clashes continue to impact health facilities and emergency services.
articles.description: World Health Organization says more than 320,000 people have been displaced in Yemen fighting since August 1.

articles.headline: Sixth victim found following Washington condo dispute shooting
articles.title: Sixth victim confirmed in DC condo-related shooting in US, police say
articles.summary: A shooting on Thursday morning in Washington, DC left one person dead and six wounded in an incident linked to a condo maintenance dispute. Police identified the suspect as Matt Wade Lambert, who targeted building manager James Stuart at a VIDA Fitness gym before firing from his apartment and dying by suicide.
articles.description: Police confirm sixth victim in DC condo shooting; suspect dead after barricading himself and starting a fire.

articles.headline: Scott Bessent urges Federal Reserve against raising interest rates
articles.title: US Treasury warns against rate hikes during US-Iran war energy ‘shock’
articles.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent advised the Federal Reserve on Friday against increasing interest rates due to an energy supply shock from the conflict with Iran. The central bank recently kept rates at 3.75 to 4 percent, while upcoming meetings face pressure from rising energy costs and strong job growth.
articles.description: Despite Treasury's Scott Bessent's remarks, financial tracker CME Fed Watch forecasts rate hike in December likely.

articles.headline: Iran’s chief negotiator tells Al Jazeera ‘ball in US court’
articles.title: Iran’s chief negotiator tells Al Jazeera ‘ball in US court’
articles.description: Iran’s chief negotiator says it’s up to the US to answer Iran’s position in the latest round of peace talks.

articles.headline: Copper prices slide to four-month low amid interest rate and demand fears
articles.title: Copper prices slid to near four-month low amid fears of hike in U.S. interest rates, lower AI demand
articles.summary: Global copper prices dropped to a nearly four-month low, trading at $13,461.99 per tonne due to anticipated United States Federal Reserve interest rate hikes and declining industrial demand from China. The Federation of Indian Mineral Industries stated that the stronger dollar and investor profit booking also contributed to the downturn. Industry experts expect short-term market volatility but maintain an optimistic long-term outlook.
articles.description: According to the industry body FIMI, prices are expected to remain volatile in the short-term though they may elevate in the long-term fuelled by increased demand.

articles.headline: KPMG opens Bengaluru technology hub to target sports sector opportunities
articles.title: KPMG sets up sports tech hub to unlock India’s $40-bn sports opportunity by 2030
articles.summary: KPMG in India inaugurated its Sports Technology Hub in Bengaluru on November 13, 2026, to accelerate digital transformation and address operational challenges in the sports industry. Opened by CEO Yezdi Nagporewalla and Indian Olympic Association President P. T. Usha, the collaborative platform showcases artificial intelligence, analytics, and venue management tools designed to help sports organisations improve performance and fan engagement.
articles.description: The firm is setting up a Sports Technology Hub to accelerate digital transformation across India's sports ecosystem. The initiative brings together AI, advanced analytics, computer vision, and emerging digital technologies to enhance fan experiences, athlete performance, commercial opportunities and sports operations, says Yezdi Nagporewalla, CEO, KPMG in India

articles.headline: Protesters clash with police across Spain following housing cost rallies
articles.title: Protesters clash with police in Spain after huge housing cost rallies
articles.summary: Police deployed tear gas and rubber bullet launchers after sporadic clashes erupted in Madrid and Barcelona on Wednesday following nationwide protests over housing affordability and purchasing power. Hundreds of thousands participated in Spain's first nationwide twenty-four-hour strike since 2012, occurring weeks before an early general election set for November 29.
articles.description: The size of the demonstrations has been seen as an indicator of public discontent before a snap election set for this month, in which the right-wing opposition is expected to defeat Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez

articles.headline: ABB India reports ten percent profit rise with record quarterly orders
articles.title: ABB India Q3 profit rises 10% to ₹440 crore; orders hit record ₹4,733 crore
articles.summary: ABB India announced a ten percent year-on-year increase in net profit to four hundred forty crore rupees for the third quarter of calendar year 2026. Revenue grew nineteen percent to three thousand seven hundred thirty-eight crore rupees, while order inflows reached a record four thousand seven hundred thirty-three crore rupees. Country Managing Director Sanjeev Sharma attributed the performance to broad-based industrial demand and infrastructure investments.
articles.description: India’s structural growth drivers in industrialisation, electrification, digitalisation and the energy transition continue to support attractive growth opportunities for ABB India, Country Managing Director, Sanjeev Sharma

articles.headline: Truck and bus collision in Assam leaves twenty-four dead
articles.title: Truck and bus crash in India’s Assam state kills at least 24 people
articles.summary: At least twenty-four people were killed and eleven others injured following a head-on collision between a container truck and a bus in India's northeastern state of Assam on Friday. Police confirmed the tragedy occurred on a highway in the Golaghat district near Kaziranga National Park, prompting Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma to express deep distress over the heavy loss of life.
articles.description: Several children and the bus driver were among those killed, officials said, with the death toll expected to rise.

articles.headline: Amnesty International criticises UN and South Sudan over village massacre
articles.title: Amnesty says UN, South Sudan officials failed to prevent village massacre
articles.summary: Amnesty International stated that United Nations peacekeepers and South Sudanese authorities failed to act on warnings before armed men attacked an Abiemnom village and killed more than 200 people. Tigere Chagutah, Amnesty's director for East and Southern Africa, said Thursday that stronger preventive action could have saved lives ahead of the upcoming December 22 elections.
articles.description: Peacekeepers knew of likely raid on Abiemnom, where more than 200 people were killed, according to rights group report.

articles.headline: Pinarayi Vijayan demands judicial inquiry into Keralam power deal controversy
articles.title: Keralam Electricity Minister’s statements on GNA deal disprove CM’s claims, says Pinarayi Vijayan
articles.summary: Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan has called for a judicial inquiry into the cancelled GNA power purchase deal. He stated that Electricity Minister Sunny Joseph’s recent remarks contradict the Chief Minister’s previous claims, suggesting the government misled the public. Vijayan argued these discrepancies expose internal cabinet divisions and a lack of collective responsibility regarding the contract.
articles.description: Keralam Leader of the Opposition reiterates his demand for a judicial inquiry headed by a High Court judge into the controversy surrounding the cancellation of the power purchase deal; he asks CM Satheesan to apologise to people for ‘manufacturing a non-existent power crisis’

articles.headline: German parliament approves major overhaul granting intelligence services expanded powers
articles.title: German spies handed new powers to tackle 'hybrid threats' from abroad
articles.summary: The Bundestag in Germany approved legislation granting foreign and domestic intelligence services expanded powers to counter hybrid threats, espionage, and sabotage. Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt championed the reforms in response to foreign powers, whereas opposition politicians criticized the measures by comparing them to secret police authorities.
articles.description: German reforms mean foreign and domestic intelligence services will have greater powers to combat espionage, terrorism and sabotage.

articles.headline: Democrats hold leverage to strip US-Israel military integration from Pentagon bill
articles.title: Will Democrats try to strip US-Israel initiative from Pentagon funding?
articles.summary: Advocates state that Democratic lawmakers possess the congressional leverage necessary to remove a controversial measure from the National Defense Authorization Act before a December 11 funding deadline. Section 219 of the Senate bill establishes the United States-Israel Defense Technology Cooperation Initiative. Critics warn this bypasses congressional oversight, while progressive groups urge party leaders to block the legislation until the integration provision is completely eliminated.
articles.description: Midterm gains give party room to overhaul NDAA funding, including provision to integrate US-Israeli military industries.

articles.headline: Aaditya Thackeray urges establishment of central and state climate councils
articles.title: Aaditya Thackeray calls for Climate Change Councils at Centre, State levels to tackle pollution
articles.summary: Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray has proposed creating Climate Change Councils at the central and state levels to improve pollution monitoring and policy coordination. Writing on social media, the former Maharashtra environment minister criticised the central government for alleged greenwashing and unreliable statistics. He warned that worsening environmental degradation threatens India's economy, national security, and public health.
articles.description: At the State level, he proposed similar councils chaired by the respective Chief Ministers, with participation from relevant departments to monitor the implementation of climate action plans

articles.headline: Former Madras High Court judge C.S. Karnan passes away in Chennai
articles.title: C.S. Karnan, controversial former High Court judge, passes away in Chennai
articles.summary: Controversial former Madras High Court judge C.S. Karnan died on November 13, 2026, at a private hospital in Chennai at age 71. Appointed in 2009, he later served at the Calcutta High Court, where he received a six-month prison sentence for contempt in 2017 following public confrontations with Supreme Court judges regarding caste discrimination.
articles.description: He was sentenced to six months of imprisonment during his stint as a judge of Calcutta High Court in 2017 after he passed an “order” sentencing the then CJI and seven other Supreme Court judges to five years of imprisonment

articles.headline: Survey maps butterfly diversity in Silent Valley National Park
articles.title: Survey begins to map butterfly diversity in Keralam’s Silent Valley
articles.summary: Researchers and volunteers launched a three-day butterfly survey at Silent Valley National Park in Palakkad to evaluate forest health and habitat conditions. Organised by the Kerala Forests and Wildlife department and the Malabar Natural History Society, teams are covering fourteen locations to document species distribution and host plants. The findings will update existing records and guide future conservation strategies for the region.
articles.description: The survey, organised jointly by the Kerala Forests and Wildlife department and the Malabar Natural History Society, will continue until November 15

articles.headline: Experts discuss resilient blue economy at Indian Academy of Sciences meeting
articles.title: Experts place emphasis on ‘resilient blue economy’
articles.summary: Experts at the 92nd Indian Academy of Sciences meeting in Thiruvananthapuram highlighted the need for a resilient blue economy to ensure sustainable growth. Ministry of Earth Sciences Secretary Srinivasa Kumar Tummala noted that Mission Mausam is expanding radar networks to improve weather forecasting, while researchers emphasized addressing climate-related hazards and gaps in marine resource mapping.
articles.description: 92nd annual meeting of the Indian Academy of Sciences opens at National Centre for Earth Science Studies, Thiruvananthapuram

articles.headline: Keralam to launch Jeeva-Suyathra road safety mission on November 15
articles.title: ‘Jeeva-Suyathra’ Mission to reduce road accidents in Keralam; State-level launch on November 15
articles.summary: Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan will inaugurate the Jeeva-Suyathra Mission in Ernakulam on November 15 to improve road safety. The state-level campaign aims to reduce accident fatalities and injuries by 50% by 2030. The initiative focuses on safer infrastructure, improved emergency responses, and public awareness programs involving local institutions, students, and the general public across the state.
articles.description: The State government has conceived the initiative with the prime objective of reducing road accident fatalities and injuries by half by 2030

articles.headline: Revanth Reddy criticizes BJP opposition to Rahul Gandhi’s summit participation
articles.title: Why spew venom on LoP Rahul Gandhi? Revanth asks BJP
articles.summary: Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy condemned the Bharatiya Janata Party for opposing Congress leader Rahul Gandhi’s attendance at the Bharat Summit. Speaking in Hyderabad, Reddy argued that democratic traditions require welcoming opposition leaders at international forums. He criticized the BJP for labeling Gandhi anti-national and warned against planned protests during the upcoming event in Hyderabad.
articles.description: The Chief Minister urged the BJP to participate in Bharat Summit and recalled Rajiv Gandhi’s decision to include then LoP Vajpayee in Indian delegation

articles.headline: Passenger vehicle wholesales reach record 5 lakh units in October
articles.title: PV wholesales cross 5 lakh units in October, up 12% YoY: SIAM
articles.summary: Domestic passenger vehicle wholesales reached a record 5.19 lakh units in October, marking a 12.4% increase compared to the previous year, according to the Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers. Two-wheeler and three-wheeler sales also saw significant growth. Industry officials attributed the positive performance to strong demand, improved credit availability, and rapid electrification in the three-wheeler segment.
articles.description: “The Indian automobile industry continues to witness healthy demand momentum,” said Rajesh Menon, Director General, SIAM.

articles.headline: First information report registered against Mamata Banerjee over remarks
articles.title: FIR against former CM Mamata Banerjee over alleged communal remarks in Bengal
articles.summary: A police case was filed against former West Bengal Chief Minister and Trinamool Congress supremo Mamata Banerjee concerning alleged communal statements made during a campaign. According to a senior police official, the initial zero FIR was registered on June 7, 2026, following a complaint by Tushar Kanti Das, and was later transferred to the Hare Street police station.
articles.description: During a protest against the SIR, the TMC chief allegedly told a minority community that their safety depended on her, advising them not to pay heed to the BJP’s ‘misleading’ words

articles.headline: Indonesian VP resigns over education qualification row
articles.title: Indonesian VP resigns over education qualification row
articles.description: Indonesia's Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka has resigned amid a dispute over his educational qualifications.

articles.headline: Nvidia chief Jensen Huang faces scrutiny amid spy allegations against associate
articles.title: How Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's extramarital affair could cause collateral damage in Washington
articles.summary: Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang faces escalating scrutiny after allegations that a Chinese businesswoman he associated with engaged in espionage. U.S. authorities have launched investigations into the cloud computing firm Megaspeed, while President Donald Trump stated he spoke with Huang about the controversy. The developments arrive as Nvidia remains central to artificial intelligence infrastructure and U.S. economic strategies, prompting bipartisan calls for congressional probes.
articles.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang confronts a widening political and legal storm in Washington over an alleged extramarital affair and claims a former Megaspeed executive spied for China, as federal investigators probe export controls and possible national-security breaches tied to Nvidia’s chips in the high-stakes U.S.-China AI race

articles.headline: Anthropic tests consumer AI agent Duet for professionals and small business owners
articles.title: Claude’s Duet agent is a little neurotic and surprisingly helpful
articles.summary: Anthropic has released a research preview of Claude Duet, a consumer artificial intelligence agent designed to assist professionals and small business owners in the United States who subscribe to Pro, Max, and Ultra tiers. Operating through a dedicated application on the iPhone Duo, the tool integrates work emails, calendars, Google Documents, and Slack to manage daily schedules and suggest tasks.
articles.description: Normally, the products I test don't offer to help me write up my experience with them. Duet is different. Claude Duet is Anthropic's AI agent for consumers, the latest attempt by an AI company to try to convince us that agents can be useful for people who don't write code. It's been an interesting couple […]

articles.headline: Americans vote in midterm elections determining presidential power
articles.title: U.S. midterm election results 2026: List of key winners
articles.summary: Americans went to the polls on November 3, 2026, in midterm elections that will determine how much power United States President Donald Trump retains for the remainder of his term. Voters decided all 435 seats in the House of Representatives, 35 Senate seats, and 36 state governorships. Over 210 million registered citizens were eligible to cast ballots across the country as voting concluded.
articles.description: All 435 seats in the House of Representatives, 35 of the 100 Senate seats, and governorships in 36 states went for election, with about 210 million people registered to vote

articles.headline: Razorpay receives market regulator approval for initial public offering
articles.title: Indian fintech firm Razorpay gets regulatory nod for IPO
articles.summary: Indian financial technology firm Razorpay has secured the Securities and Exchange Board of India approval for an initial public offering potentially valued at approximately $600 million. Founded in 2014 and backed by investors including Y Combinator and Singapore sovereign wealth fund, the Bengaluru-based company processes online payments through cards, net banking, Unified Payments Interface, and digital wallets.
articles.description: In June, the Bengaluru-based ‌firm confidentially filed draft ‌papers ⁠for IPO likely ⁠sized at around $600 million

articles.headline: Democrat Scott Colom defeats Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi Senate race
articles.title: Mississippi elects Democrat Scott Colom as state's first Black U.S. senator since Reconstruction
articles.summary: Democratic nominee Scott Colom defeated Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi's closely contested United States Senate race. The prolonged ballot count concluded with the local prosecutor winning the election, making him the state's first Black senator since Reconstruction. This historic outcome adds to a decisive midterm rebuke against the political party of President Donald Trump.
articles.description: Former President Bill Clinton and former Vice-President Kamala Harris campaigned on Scott Colom's behalf in the campaign's closing weeks

articles.headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang departs company following extramarital affair investigations
